> 1: # PLAN.md

**Prompt 79:**
> Pulse: Service Status and Incident Hub
> 2: 
> 3: ## 1. Problem and users
> 4: 
> 5: Chosen problem: Option 1

**Prompt 80:**
> Pulse.
> 6: 
> 7: Pulse helps three groups:
> 8: 
> 9: - Service owners / on-call engineers: detect service failures quickly and manage incident response.
> 10: - Support team: understand which services are affected and whether an incident is ongoing.
> 11: - Customers: see a clear, read-only status page instead of guessing whether a failed payment or claim is caused by the platform.
> 12: 
> 13: The outcome that matters: detect service failures, track recovery, and communicate the current state to operators and customers.
> 14: 
> 15: ## 2. Why Pulse
> 16: 
> 17: Pulse is the lower-risk choice for a six-hour solo build. The starter kit supplies four mock services (quotes, payments, claims, notifications), health endpoints, controls to simulate down/slow/flaky behaviour, a webhook receiver, and an incident drill script. The core product can therefore be demonstrated through real HTTP checks without building a container deployment system.
> 18: 
> 19: Launchpad requires image builds, registry pushes, container deployments, two environments, health validation, automatic rollback, manual rollback, and environment-specific configuration. That creates more integration risk within six hours.
> 20: 
> 21: ## 3. Discovery: questions for the product owner
> 22: 
> 23: Ask these during the first 15 minutes. Record the actual answers here; do not invent answers.
> 24: 
> 25: | Question | Default if no answer is available |
> 26: |---|---|
> 27: | What response-time threshold separates healthy from degraded? | HTTP 2xx under 1.5 seconds is healthy; slower 2xx is degraded. |
> 28: | How many consecutive failures should open an incident? | Two consecutive failed checks; the first failure marks the service degraded. |
> 29: | How many successful checks are needed to resolve an incident? | Two consecutive healthy checks. |
> 30: | What availability window should the dashboard show? | Rolling 24 hours, labelled as a sampled estimate. |
> 31: | What SLO target should new services use? | 99.9%, editable per service. |
> 32: | What webhook payload or authentication does the supplied receiver expect? | Inspect its README and send the smallest compatible JSON payload. |
> 33: | Is it acceptable to extend the supplied Docker Compose setup? | Yes; keep the supplied mock services intact and add Pulse to the same runnable setup where practical. |
> 34: 
> 35: ## 4. Similar-product research
> 36: 
> 37: Spend no more than five minutes reviewing the user-facing patterns of UptimeRobot, Better Stack, or Atlassian Statuspage. Record only patterns that directly inform this MVP:
> 38: 
> 39: - A service list with a clear current-state indicator.
> 40: - An incident history with opened, acknowledged, updated, and resolved events.
> 41: - A customer-facing status page separate from the operator controls.
> 42: - Availability and response-time measurements over a defined time window.
> 43: 
> 44: Do not copy their full feature scope. The six-hour build focuses on the end-to-end health-to-incident-to-recovery workflow.
> 45: 
> 46: ## 5. MoSCoW scope
> 47: 
> 48: ### Must have
> 49: 
> 50: - Service catalogue API and UI: name, health URL, owner, check interval, and SLO target.
> 51: - Independent periodic HTTP health checks; one slow service must not block checks for others.
> 52: - Persist each check result, including timestamp, HTTP status, latency, and classified state/error.
> 53: - Consistent HEALTHY, DEGRADED, and DOWN state transitions, including recovery.
> 54: - Automatically open an incident when a service becomes DOWN; resolve it after recovery.
> 55: - Incident acknowledgement, operator notes, and a chronological event timeline.
> 56: - Operator dashboard showing current states, latest response times, and active/recent incidents.
> 57: - Read-only public status page showing current state and recent incident history.
> 58: - One-command startup instructions and a README that documents the working features and limitations.
> 59: 
> 60: ### Should have
> 61: 
> 62: - Webhook notification when an incident opens and when it resolves.
> 63: - Rolling 24-hour availability estimate, configured SLO, estimated error budget remaining, MTTD, and MTTR.
> 64: - Basic service and incident filters.
> 65: 
> 66: ### Could have
> 67: 
> 68: - Small response-time history chart.
> 69: - Incident filtering by date and service.
> 70: - Edit/pause service monitoring.
> 71: 
> 72: ### Won't have in this build
> 73: 
> 74: - Authentication, roles, and customer subscriptions.
> 75: - AI-generated incident summaries.
> 76: - Email/SMS integrations, Kubernetes, non-HTTP probes, or complex alert routing.
> 77: - Distributed workers, Redis, Celery, or a separate monitoring stack.
> 78: 
> 79: If time is short, finish the core workflow first. Keep notifications and metrics simple rather than sacrificing detection, incident tracking, or recovery.
> 80: 
> 81: ## 6. System design
> 82: 
> 83: ### Proposed architecture
> 84: 
> 85: ```
> 86: Mock services (quotes, payments, claims, notifications)
> 87:               ^
> 88:               | asynchronous HTTP health checks
> 89:               |
> 90:        FastAPI backend
> 91:        |      |       |
> 92:    Scheduler State  Incident + webhook logic
> 93:        |      |       |
> 94:        +--- SQLite database
> 95:               |
> 96:         REST API endpoints
> 97:               |
> 98:         React dashboard
> 99:           /        \
> 100:  Operator view   Public status page
> 101: ```
> 102: 
> 103: ### Technology choices
> 104: 
> 105: - Backend: Python + FastAPI.
> 106: - Health probes: httpx asynchronous client with per-request timeouts and concurrent checks.
> 107: - Scheduling: one lightweight asyncio background loop that selects services due for a check. Avoid Celery/Redis.
> 108: - Database: SQLite for the six-hour MVP.
> 109: - Frontend: React + Vite; keep styling simple and prioritize readable status and incident information.
> 110: - Runtime: Docker Compose, reusing the provided mock services and webhook receiver.
> 111: 
> 112: ### State rules (initial defaults; update if the product owner specifies otherwise)
> 113: 
> 114: - HTTP 2xx with latency below 1.5 seconds: HEALTHY.
> 115: - HTTP 2xx with latency at or above 1.5 seconds: DEGRADED.
> 116: - First timeout/non-2xx result: DEGRADED.
> 117: - Two consecutive timeout/non-2xx results: DOWN; open one active incident if one does not already exist.
> 118: - Two consecutive healthy results after DOWN: HEALTHY; resolve the active incident and emit a recovery event.
> 119: - A slow but successful result remains DEGRADED; it does not count as a healthy recovery result.
> 120: - Run checks concurrently and apply a timeout so a slow dependency cannot stall other services.
> 121: 
> 122: ### Initial data model
> 123: 
> 124: - Service: id, name, slug, health_url, owner, interval_seconds, slo_target, enabled, current_state, created_at.
> 125: - HealthCheck: id, service_id, checked_at, http_status, latency_ms, state, error_message.
> 126: - Incident: id, service_id, opened_at, resolved_at, status, acknowledged_at, acknowledged_by.
> 127: - IncidentEvent: id, incident_id, event_type, message, created_at.
> 128: 
> 129: Store operator notes as incident events so the timeline is the single source of truth for incident activity.
> 130:

> 219: ## 10. Test plan and success metrics
> 220: 
> 221: ### Unit tests
> 222: 
> 223: - Healthy, degraded, and failed response classification.
> 224: - Consecutive failure and recovery thresholds.
> 225: - No duplicate active incidents for one service.
> 226: - Availability, MTTD, MTTR, and error-budget calculations.
> 227: 
> 228: ### Integration tests
> 229: 
> 230: - Health check calls a mock /health endpoint and persists the result.
> 231: - A down service opens an incident and sends a webhook.
> 232: - A recovered service resolves the incident and sends a recovery webhook.
> 233: - A slow service does not block checks for other services.
> 234: 
> 235: ### Acceptance test
> 236: 
> 237: 1. Start the complete application and supplied mock services.
> 238: 2. Confirm all four services initially show healthy.
> 239: 3. Trigger the Payments service /control/down endpoint.
> 240: 4. Wait for the configured failure threshold; confirm DOWN, an open incident, timeline entry, and webhook notification.
> 241: 5. Acknowledge the incident and add a note.
> 242: 6. Trigger /control/reset.
> 243: 7. Wait for the recovery threshold; confirm HEALTHY, resolved incident, recovery event, and updated public status page.
> 244: 
> 245: ### Product metrics
> 246: 
> 247: - Detection delay / MTTD.
> 248: - Mean time to recovery / MTTR.
> 249: - Sampled availability over the rolling 24-hour window versus the service SLO.
> 250: - Mean/latest health-check response time and failed-check count.
> 251: - Webhook delivery success/failure count.
> 252: 
> 253: ## 11. Explicit assumptions and risks
> 254: 
> 255: - The supplied starter kit and mock services are available and can be run locally.
> 256: - The MVP uses periodic HTTP probes; availability and error-budget values are sampled estimates.
> 257: - SQLite is sufficient for a local single-operator demo.
> 258: - No authentication is included; the operator dashboard is for the local demo only.
> 259: - If frontend work takes longer than expected, keep the public page minimal and finish incident lifecycle, webhook, tests, and runnable setup first.
> 260: - Do not introduce Redis, Celery, Kubernetes, or a separate observability stack during the hackathon.
> 261: 
> 262: ## 12. Demo script
> 263: 
> 264: Show the dashboard with all four services healthy. Trigger the Payments mock service's down control. Show Pulse detect the failure, change the state, open an incident, and send a webhook. Acknowledge the incident and add an operator note. Reset Payments. Show Pulse detect recovery, resolve the incident, and update the public page and metrics.
> 265: 
> 266: The demo is successful when the failure-to-recovery lifecycle works end to end without manually editing the database or refreshing service state by hand.

> 1: # PLAN.md

**Prompt 216:**
> Pulse: Service Status and Incident Hub
> 2: 
> 3: ## 1. Problem and users
> 4: 
> 5: **Chosen problem: Option 1

**Prompt 217:**
> Pulse.**
> 6: 
> 7: Pulse helps three groups:
> 8: - **Service owners / on-call engineers:** detect service failures quickly and manage incident response.
> 9: - **Support team:** understand which services are affected and whether an incident is ongoing.
> 10: - **Customers:** see a clear, read-only status page instead of guessing whether a failed payment or claim is caused by the platform.
> 11: 
> 12: The outcome that matters: detect service failures, track recovery, and communicate the current state to operators and customers.
> 13: 
> 14: ## 2. Why Pulse
> 15: 
> 16: Pulse is the lower-risk choice for a six-hour solo build. The starter kit supplies four mock services (`quotes`, `payments`, `claims`, `notifications`), health endpoints, controls to simulate down/slow/flaky behaviour, a webhook receiver, and an incident drill script. The core product can therefore be demonstrated through real HTTP checks without building a container deployment system.
> 17: 
> 18: Launchpad requires image builds, registry pushes, container deployments, two environments, health validation, automatic rollback, manual rollback, and environment-specific configuration. That creates more integration risk within six hours.
> 19: 
> 20: ## 3. Discovery: questions for the product owner
> 21: 
> 22: Ask these during the first 15 minutes. Record the actual answers here; do not invent answers.
> 23: 
> 24: | Question | Default if no answer is available |
> 25: |---|---|
> 26: | What response-time threshold separates healthy from degraded? | HTTP 2xx under 1.5 seconds is healthy; slower 2xx is degraded. |
> 27: | How many consecutive failures should open an incident? | Two consecutive failed checks; the first failure marks the service degraded. |
> 28: | How many successful checks are needed to resolve an incident? | Two consecutive healthy checks. |
> 29: | What availability window should the dashboard show? | Rolling 24 hours, labelled as a sampled estimate. |
> 30: | What SLO target should new services use? | 99.9%, editable per service. |
> 31: | What webhook payload or authentication does the supplied receiver expect? | Inspect its README and send the smallest compatible JSON payload. |
> 32: | Is it acceptable to extend the supplied Docker Compose setup? | Yes; keep the supplied mock services intact and add Pulse to the same runnable setup where practical. |
> 33: 
> 34: ## 4. Similar-product research
> 35: 
> 36: Spend no more than five minutes reviewing the user-facing patterns of UptimeRobot, Better Stack, or Atlassian Statuspage. Record only patterns that directly inform this MVP:
> 37: - A service list with a clear current-state indicator.
> 38: - An incident history with opened, acknowledged, updated, and resolved events.
> 39: - A customer-facing status page separate from the operator controls.
> 40: - Availability and response-time measurements over a defined time window.
> 41: 
> 42: Do not copy their full feature scope. The six-hour build focuses on the end-to-end health-to-incident-to-recovery workflow.
> 43: 
> 44: ## 5. MoSCoW scope
> 45: 
> 46: ### Must have
> 47: - Service catalogue API and UI: name, health URL, owner, check interval, and SLO target.
> 48: - Independent periodic HTTP health checks; one slow service must not block checks for others.
> 49: - Persist each check result, including timestamp, HTTP status, latency, and classified state/error.
> 50: - Consistent `HEALTHY`, `DEGRADED`, and `DOWN` state transitions, including recovery.
> 51: - Automatically open an incident when a service becomes `DOWN`; resolve it after recovery.
> 52: - Incident acknowledgement, operator notes, and a chronological event timeline.
> 53: - Operator dashboard showing current states, latest response times, and active/recent incidents.
> 54: - Read-only public status page showing current state and recent incident history.
> 55: - One-command startup instructions and a README that documents the working features and limitations.
> 56: 
> 57: ### Should have
> 58: - Webhook notification when an incident opens and when it resolves.
> 59: - Rolling 24-hour availability estimate, configured SLO, estimated error budget remaining, MTTD, and MTTR.
> 60: - Basic service and incident filters.
> 61: 
> 62: ### Could have
> 63: - Small response-time history chart.
> 64: - Incident filtering by date and service.
> 65: - Edit/pause service monitoring.
> 66: 
> 67: ### Won't have in this build
> 68: - Authentication, roles, and customer subscriptions.
> 69: - AI-generated incident summaries.
> 70: - Email/SMS integrations, Kubernetes, non-HTTP probes, or complex alert routing.
> 71: - Distributed workers, Redis, Celery, or a separate monitoring stack.
> 72: 
> 73: If time is short, finish the core workflow first. Keep notifications and metrics simple rather than sacrificing detection, incident tracking, or recovery.
> 74: 
> 75: ## 6. System design
> 76: 
> 77: ### Proposed architecture
> 78: 
> 79: ```text
> 80: Mock services (quotes, payments, claims, notifications)
> 81:               ^
> 82:               | asynchronous HTTP health checks
> 83:               |
> 84:        FastAPI backend
> 85:        |      |       |
> 86:    Scheduler State  Incident + webhook logic
> 87:        |      |       |
> 88:        +--- SQLite database
> 89:               |
> 90:         REST API endpoints
> 91:               |
> 92:         React dashboard
> 93:           /        \
> 94:  Operator view   Public status page
> 95: ```
> 96: 
> 97: ### Technology choices
> 98: - **Backend:** Python + FastAPI.
> 99: - **Health probes:** `httpx` asynchronous client with per-request timeouts and concurrent checks.
> 100: - **Scheduling:** one lightweight `asyncio` background loop that selects services due for a check. Avoid Celery/Redis.
> 101: - **Database:** SQLite for the six-hour MVP.
> 102: - **Frontend:** React + Vite; keep styling simple and prioritize readable status and incident information.
> 103: - **Runtime:** Docker Compose, reusing the provided mock services and webhook receiver.
> 104: 
> 105: ### State rules (initial defaults; update if the product owner specifies otherwise)
> 106: - HTTP 2xx with latency below 1.5 seconds: `HEALTHY`.
> 107: - HTTP 2xx with latency at or above 1.5 seconds: `DEGRADED`.
> 108: - First timeout/non-2xx result: `DEGRADED`.
> 109: - Two consecutive timeout/non-2xx results: `DOWN`; open one active incident if one does not already exist.
> 110: - Two consecutive healthy results after `DOWN`: `HEALTHY`; resolve the active incident and emit a recovery event.
> 111: - A slow but successful result remains `DEGRADED`; it does not count as a healthy recovery result.
> 112: - Run checks concurrently and apply a timeout so a slow dependency cannot stall other services.
> 113: 
> 114: ### Initial data model
> 115: 
> 116: - **Service:** `id`, `name`, `slug`, `health_url`, `owner`, `interval_seconds`, `slo_target`, `enabled`, `current_state`, `created_at`.
> 117: - **HealthCheck:** `id`, `service_id`, `checked_at`, `http_status`, `latency_ms`, `state`, `error_message`.
> 118: - **Incident:** `id`, `service_id`, `opened_at`, `resolved_at`, `status`, `acknowledged_at`, `acknowledged_by`.
> 119: - **IncidentEvent:** `id`, `incident_id`, `event_type`, `message`, `created_at`.
> 120:

> 26: Single process. One asyncio loop runs the web app, the scheduler and webhook sender tasks. No Redis, Celery or workers.
> 27: 
> 28: ## 2. Components
> 29: 
> 30: | Component | Responsibility | Pure/IO | Unit |
> 31: |---|---|---|---|
> 32: | Config | Read env: DB path, timeout, thresholds, webhook URL | IO (startup) | U0 |
> 33: | Clock | `now()` in UTC, injectable in tests | pure | U1 |
> 34: | DB layer | aiosqlite, WAL, one write path, transactions | IO | U1 |
> 35: | Catalogue | Register/list services, validation | IO | U1 |
> 36: | Scheduler | Pick due services, run checks concurrently, update `next_check_at` | IO | U2 |
> 37: | Probe | One httpx request with timeout, returns result record | IO | U2 |
> 38: | Classifier | Result + counters -> new state, counters, incident action | **pure** | U3 |
> 39: | Incident store | Apply classifier output in one transaction, enforce one active incident | IO | U3 |
> 40: | Webhook sender | Background task, bounded retries, delivery records | IO | U6 |
> 41: | Metrics | Availability, budget, MTTD, MTTR, checker perf | **pure** | U6 |
> 42: | Operator UI | Server-rendered pages under `/ops` | IO | U4 |

> 48: 
> 49: ```
> 50: scheduler loop (every tick)
> 51:

> 52:

**Prompt 240:**
> in ONE transaction per service:
> 55:             1. insert health_check row (with lag + duration)
> 56:             2. classify(result, counters) -> new state, counters, incident action
> 57:             3. update service (state, counters, first_failure_at, next_check_at)
> 58:             4. open / resolve incident + insert incident_event

> 62: 
> 63: Rules that matter:
> 64: - Result, counters, state, incident and next_check_at are written in one transaction, so a crash cannot cause a double check or a half-applied transition.
> 65: - The webhook is never awaited inside the check path. Pending delivery rows make it restart-safe.
> 66: - One delivery per (incident, event) via a unique constraint, so a restart or race cannot duplicate it.
> 67: - One active incident per service via a partial unique index.
> 68: 
> 69: ## 4. State model
> 70: 
> 71: States: `HEALTHY`, `DEGRADED`, `DOWN`.
> 72: 
> 73: Inputs: fast success, slow success, non-2xx, timeout, connection error, restart.
> 74: 
> 75: The rules (what counts as failed, degraded latency, failures to DOWN, recovery count, reopen behaviour) are defined only in `DECISIONS.md`. The full transition table lives in `docs/TESTS.md` under "State machine table". Every row has a test.
> 76: 
> 77: Open points to decide first: **(D-?)** failed-check definition and timeout, **(D-?)** degraded latency, **(D-?)** failures to DOWN, **(D-?)** recovery rule and whether a slow success counts, **(D-?)** reopen vs new incident, **(D-?)** whether DEGRADED opens an incident.
> 78: 
> 79: ## 5. Data model
> 80: 
> 81: Starts from PLAN.md section 6, extended with what Units 1-6 need so no migration is required later.
> 82: 
> 83: **service**: id, name (unique), slug, health_url (unique), owner, interval_seconds, slo_target, enabled, current_state, consecutive_failures, consecutive_successes, first_failure_at, next_check_at, created_at
> 84: 
> 85: **health_check**: id, service_id, scheduled_at, started_at, checked_at, duration_ms, http_status (nullable), latency_ms (nullable), state, error_message (nullable)
> 86: 
> 87: **incident**: id, service_id, opened_at, resolved_at (nullable), status (active/resolved), acknowledged_at, acknowledged_by, title
> 88: - Partial unique index: one row per service where `status = 'active'`.
> 89: 
> 90: **incident_event**: id, incident_id, event_type (opened, acknowledged, note_added, resolved), message, created_at
> 91: - Operator notes are events; the timeline is the single source of truth.
> 92: 
> 93: **webhook_delivery**: id, incident_id, event_type, attempt, outcome, response_code, created_at, plus an idempotency key unique per (incident_id, event_type) for the logical event.
> 94: 
> 95: **checker_stats** (or derived): skipped runs counter, for "how the checking itself is performing".
> 96: 
> 97: All timestamps stored as UTC.

> 1: # Pulse starter kit
> 2: 
> 3: Everything you need to build **Pulse**, the status and incident hub. Read the problem statement first.
> 4: 
> 5: ## Start the kit
> 6: 
> 7: ```
> 8: docker compose up --build
> 9: ```
> 10: 
> 11: > **Using Podman?** Run `podman compose up --build` instead (needs `podman-compose` or Docker Compose installed). Everything else is the same.
> 12: 
> 13: This starts four mock Acko services and a webhook receiver:
> 14: 
> 15: | Service | Address | Health check |
> 16: | --- | --- | --- |
> 17: | `quotes` | http://localhost:7001 | http://localhost:7001/health |
> 18: | `payments` | http://localhost:7002 | http://localhost:7002/health |
> 19: | `claims` | http://localhost:7003 | http://localhost:7003/health |
> 20: | `notifications` | http://localhost:7004 | http://localhost:7004/health |
> 21: | Webhook receiver | http://localhost:9900 | Stands in for chat, email and paging. Anything POSTed to it appears on its page. `GET /api/received` returns the list as JSON; `DELETE /api/received` clears it. |
> 22: 
> 23: From inside Docker (for example, if you run Pulse in the same Compose network), use the service names instead: `http://claims:8080/health`, `http://webhook-receiver:9000`.
> 24: 
> 25: > **Port already in use?** If something on your laptop already uses port 9900, start the kit with another port for the webhook receiver, for example `WEBHOOK_PORT=9950 docker compose up --build`.
> 26: 
> 27: ## Simulating trouble
> 28: 
> 29: Each mock service has control endpoints. For example, for `claims` on port 7003:
> 30: 
> 31: | Command | Effect |
> 32: | --- | --- |
> 33: | `curl -X POST localhost:7003/control/down` | Health checks return 503 until reset |
> 34: | `curl -X POST "localhost:7003/control/slow?ms=3000"` | Health checks succeed, but only after 3 seconds |
> 35: | `curl -X POST "localhost:7003/control/flaky?rate=0.3"` | Health checks fail at random, 30% of the time |
> 36: | `curl -X POST localhost:7003/control/reset` | Back to normal |
> 37: | `curl localhost:7003/control/state` | Shows the current mode |
> 38: 
> 39: ## The incident drill
> 40: 
> 41: `scripts/incident-drill.sh` breaks and repairs the services on a fixed schedule, so you can test Pulse and run a repeatable demo:
> 42: 
> 43: ```
> 44: bash scripts/incident-drill.sh          # full drill, about 7 minutes
> 45: bash scripts/incident-drill.sh --fast   # short drill, under 3 minutes
> 46: bash scripts/incident-drill.sh --reset  # put every service back to normal
> 47: ```
> 48: 
> 49: ## Rules
> 50: 
> 51: - You may configure and run the kit however you like, but **don't change the mock services or the webhook receiver**: the evaluators test your product against the original kit.

> 7: POST /control/slow?ms=3000      health answers successfully, but only after the delay
> 8: POST /control/flaky?rate=0.3    health fails at random with the given probability (0 to 1)
> 9: POST /control/reset             back to normal
> 10: 
> 11: Do not change this file: the evaluators test against the original kit.
> 12: """

> 14: import os
> 15: import random
> 16: import threading
> 17: import time

> 33:         self.send_response(code)

> 35:         self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
> 36:         self.end_headers()
> 37:         self.wfile.write(data)
> 38:

> 40:         print(f"{SERVICE} {self.command} {self.path} {args[1] if len(args) > 1 else ''}", flush=True)
> 41:

> 1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
> 2: # Incident drill: breaks and repairs the mock services on a fixed schedule,
> 3: # so you can test Pulse and run a repeatable demo.
> 4: #   bash scripts/incident-drill.sh          full drill (about 7 minutes)
> 5: #   bash scripts/incident-drill.sh --fast   short drill (under 3 minutes)
> 6: #   bash scripts/incident-drill.sh --reset  put every service back to normal
> 7: set -eu
> 8: HOST="${HOST:-localhost}"
> 9: port() { case "$1" in quotes) echo 7001;; payments) echo 7002;; claims) echo 7003;; notifications) echo 7004;; esac; }
> 10: UNIT=60
> 11: [ "${1:-}" = "--fast" ] && UNIT=20
> 12: 
> 13: ctl() { # service action [query]
> 14:   curl -fsS -X POST "http://$HOST:$(port "$1")/control/$2${3:+?$3}" >/dev/null && \
> 15:   echo "$(date +%H:%M:%S)  $1 -> $2${3:+ ($3)}"
> 16: }
> 17: reset_all() { for s in quotes payments claims notifications; do ctl "$s" reset; done; }
> 18: 
> 19: if [ "${1:-}" = "--reset" ]; then reset_all; exit 0; fi
> 20:

**Prompt 656:**
> # Problem Statement: Option 1

**Prompt 657:**
> Pulse (Service Status and Incident Hub)
> 
> ## The Problem
> Modern distributed systems consist of numerous independent services. When failures, slowdowns, or flakiness occur, engineering teams, support staff, and customers need fast and transparent visibility:
> - **Service owners / on-call engineers:** detect service failures rapidly, monitor latency, and coordinate incident response.
> - **Support team:** understand immediately which services are impaired to communicate accurately with users.
> - **Customers:** view a trustworthy, public, read-only status page without exposing internal infrastructure details or error logs.
> 
> ## Core Capabilities Required
> 1. **Service Catalogue:** Register and manage services with HTTP health URLs, owner details, check intervals, and target SLOs.
> 2. **Health Check Prober:** Asynchronously probe services concurrently with robust timeouts so that one slow service never delays checks for others.
> 3. **State Classification & State Transitions:**
>    - HEALTHY: HTTP 2xx and response time < 1.5s
>    - DEGRADED: HTTP 2xx with latency >= 1.5s, or single failed check
>    - DOWN: 2 consecutive failures
>    - RECOVERY: 2 consecutive healthy checks (< 1.5s)
> 4. **Automated Incident Lifecycle:**
>    - Automatically open an incident when a service is DOWN.
>    - Enforce at most one active incident per service.
>    - Allow operator acknowledgement and notes.
>    - Automatically resolve the incident upon verified recovery.
> 5. **Real-time Notifications:** Webhook delivery on incident opened and incident resolved.
> 6. **Reliability Metrics:** Rolling 24-hour availability estimate, remaining error budget, MTTD (Mean Time to Detect), MTTR (Mean Time to Resolve), and checker performance (lag and duration).
> 7. **Dual-Audience Dashboards:**
>    - Operator Dashboard (`/ops`): Live health status, latency, incident timeline, acknowledgement, notes, and service management.
>    - Public Status Page (`/status`): Customer-facing, high-level status and incident history, strictly sanitised with zero data leaks (no health URLs, no owners, no internal stack traces).

health_url TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    owner TEXT NOT NULL,\n    interval_seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 10,\n    slo_target REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 99.9,\n    enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    current_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'HEALTHY',\n    consecutive_failures INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n    consecutive_successes INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n    first_failure_at TEXT,\n    next_check_at TEXT,\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS health_checks (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    scheduled_at TEXT NOT NULL,\n    started_at TEXT NOT NULL,\n    checked_at TEXT NOT NULL,\n    duration_ms INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    http_status INTEGER,\n    latency_ms INTEGER,\n    state TEXT NOT NULL,\n    error_message TEXT\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_health_checks_service_checked ON health_checks(service_id, checked_at);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS incidents (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    opened_at TEXT NOT NULL,\n    resolved_at TEXT,\n    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',\n    acknowledged_at TEXT,\n    acknowledged_by TEXT,\n    title TEXT NOT NULL\n);\n\n-- Partial unique index enforcing exactly one active incident per service\nCREATE    incident_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES incidents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    event_type TEXT NOT NULL,\n    message TEXT NOT NULL,\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_incident_events_incident_id ON incident_events(incident_id, created_at);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS webhook_deliveries (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    incident_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES incidents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    event_type TEXT NOT NULL,\n    attempt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    outcome TEXT NOT NULL,\n    response_code INTEGER,\n    idempotency_key > {"Content":"import os\nfrom contextlib import asynccontextmanager\nfrom pathlib import Path\nimport aiosqlite\nfrom src.pulse.config import settings\n\nSCHEMA_PATH = Path(__file__).parent / \"schema.sql\"\n\n\ndef get_db_path() -\u003e Path:\n    db_path = Path(settings.db_path)\n    db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    return db_path\n\n\n@asynccontextmanager\nasync def get_db():\n    \"\"\"Async context manager yielding an aiosqlite database connection.\"\"\"\n    db_path = get_db_path()\n    async with aiosqlite.connect(str(db_path)) as db:\n        db.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row\n        await db.execute(\"PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;\")\n        await db.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON;\")\n        yield db\n\n\nasync def init_db(db_file: str | Path | None = None):\n    \"\"\"Initialize database tables and indexes from schema.sql.\"\"\"\n    target_path = Path(db_file) if db_file else get_db_path()\n    target_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    \n    with open(SCHEMA_PATH, \"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n        schema = f.read()\n        \n    async with aiosqlite.connect(str(target_path)) as db:\n        await db.execute(\"PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;\")\n        await db.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON;\")\n        await db.executescript(schema)\n        await db.commit()\n","Overwrite":true,"Path":"D:/5 sem/ackopulse/src/pulse/db.py"}:

> {"Content":"import os\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom src.pulse.clock import clock\nfrom src.pulse.db import get_db\n\nDEFAULT_SERVICES = [\n    {\n        \"name\": \"Quotes Service\",\n        \"slug\": \"quotes\",\n        \"health_url\": os.environ.get(\"QUOTES_HEALTH_URL\", \"http://localhost:7001/health\"),\n        \"owner\": \"quotes-team@acko.com\",\n        \"interval_seconds\": 10,\n        \"slo_target\": 99.9,\n    },\n    {\n        \"name\": \"Payments Service\",\n        \"slug\": \"payments\",\n        \"health_url\": os.environ.get(\"PAYMENTS_HEALTH_URL\", \"http://localhost:7002/health\"),\n        \"owner\": \"payments-team@acko.com\",\n        \"interval_seconds\": 10,\n        \"slo_target\": 99.9,\n    },\n    {\n        \"name\": \"Claims Service\",\n        \"slug\": \"claims\",\n        \"health_url\": os.environ.get(\"CLAIMS_HEALTH_URL\", \"http://localhost:7003/health\"),\n        \"owner\": \"claims-team@acko.com\",\n        \"interval_seconds\": 10,\n        \"slo_target\": 99.9,\n    },\n    {\n        \"name\": \"Notifications Service\",\n        \"slug\": \"notifications\",\n        \"health_url\": os.environ.get(\"NOTIFICATIONS_HEALTH_URL\", \"http://localhost:7004/health\"),\n        \"owner\": \"notifications-team@acko.com\",\n        \"interval_seconds\": 10,\n        \"slo_target\": 99.9,\n    },\n]\n\n\nasync def seed_services(db_conn=None):\n    \"\"\"Idempotently seeds the 4 mock services into the database.\"\"\"\n    now_iso = clock.now().isoformat()\n\n    async def _do_seed(db):\n        for s in DEFAULT_SERVICES:\n            # Check if exists by slug or name\n            async with db.execute(\n                \"SELECT id FROM services WHERE slug = ? OR name = ? OR health_url = ?\",\n                (s[\"slug\"], s[\"name\"], s[\"health_url\"]),\n            ) as cursor:\n                row = await cursor.fetchone()\n                if not row:\n                    await db.execute(\n                        \"\"\"\n                        INSERT INTO services (\n                            name, slug, health_url, owner, interval_seconds, \n                            slo_target, enabled, current_state, consecutive_failures, \n                            consecutive_successes, next_check_at, created_at\n                        ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 1, 'HEALTHY', 0, 0, ?, ?)\n                        \"\"\",\n                        (\n                            s[\"name\"],\n                            s[\"slug\"],\n                            s[\"health_url\"],\n                            s[\"owner\"],\n                            s[\"interval_seconds\"],\n                            s[\"slo_target\"],\n                            now_iso,\n                            now_iso,\n                        ),\n                    )\n        await db.commit()\n\n    if db_conn:\n        await _do_seed(db_conn)\n    else:\n        async with get_db() as db:\n            await _do_seed(db)\n","Overwrite":true,"Path":"D:/5 sem/ackopulse/src/pulse/seed.py"}:

= text.lower().strip()\n    text = re.sub(r\"[^\\w\\s-]\", \"\", text)\n    return re.sub(r\"[\\s_-]+\", \"-\", text).strip(\"-\")\n\n\nclass ServiceCreate(BaseModel):\n    name: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=100)\n    slug: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=100)\n    health_url: str = Field(..., min_length=7, max_length=500)\n    owner: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=100)\n    interval_seconds: int = Field(default=10, ge=1, le=3600)\n    slo_target: float = Field(default=99.9, ge=50.0, le=100.0)\n\n    @field_validator(\"health_url\")\n    @classmethod\n    def validate_health_url(cls, v: str) -\u003e str:\n        v = v.strip()\n        parsed = urlparse(v)\n        if parsed.scheme not in (\"http\", \"https\") or not parsed.netloc:\n            raise ValueError(\"health_url must be a valid http or https URL\")\n        return v\n\n    @field_validator(\"name\", \"owner\")\n    @classmethod\n    def strip_strings(cls, v: str) -\u003e str:\n        v = v.strip()\n        if not v:\n            raise ValueError(\"Field cannot be empty or whitespace only\")\n        return v\n\n\nclass ServiceResponse(BaseModel):\n    id: int\n    name: str\n    slug: str\n    health_url: str\n    owner: str\n    interval_seconds: int\n    slo_target: float\n    enabled: bool\n    current_state: str\n    consecutive_failures: int\n    consecutive_successes: int\n    first_failure_at: str | None\n    next_check_at: str | None\n    created_at: str\n\n\nasync def list_services(db) -\u003e list[dict]:\n    async with db.execute(\n        \"\"\"\n        SELECT id, name, slug, health_url, owner, interval_seconds, slo_target,\n               enabled, current_state, consecutive_failures, consecutive_successes,\n               first_failure_at, next_check_at, created_at\n        FROM services\n        ORDER BY id ASC\n        \"\"\"\n    ) as cursor:\n        rows = await cursor.fetchall()\n        return [dict(row) for row in rows]\n\n\nasync def get_service(db, service_id: int) -\u003e dict | None:\n    async with db.execute(\n        \"\"\"\n        SELECT id, name, slug, health_url, owner, interval_seconds, slo_target,\n               enabled, current_state, consecutive_failures, consecutive_successes,\n               first_failure_at, next_check_at, created_at\n        FROM services\n        WHERE id = ?\n        \"\"\",\n        (service_id,),\n    ) as cursor:\n        row = await cursor.fetchone()\n        return dict(row) if row else None\n\n\nasync def create_service(db, data: ServiceCreate) -\u003e dict:\n    slug = data.slug or slugify(data.name)\n    now_iso = clock.now().isoformat()\n\n    # Check for duplicate name, slug, or health_url\n    async with db.execute(\n        \"SELECT id FROM services WHERE name = ? OR slug = ? OR health_url = ?\",\n        (data.name, slug, data.health_url),\n    ) as cursor:\n        existing = await cursor.fetchone()\n        if existing:\n            raise ValueError(\"A service with this name, slug, or health URL already exists\")\n\n    cursor = await db.execute(\n        \"\"\"\n        INSERT INTO services (\n            name, slug, health_url, owner, interval_seconds, slo_target,\n            enabled, current_state, consecutive_failures, consecutive_successes,\n            next_check_at, created_at\n        ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 1, 'HEALTHY', 0, 0, ?, ?)\n        \"\"\",\n        (\n            data.name,\n            slug,\n            data.health_url,\n            data.owner,\n            data.interval_seconds,\n            data.slo_target,\n            now_iso,\n            now_iso,\n        ),\n    )\n    await db.commit()\n    service_id = cursor.lastrowid\n    return await get_service(db, service_id)\n","Overwrite":true,"Path":"D:/5 sem/ackopulse/src/pulse/services.py"}:

> {"Content":"from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, status\nfrom src.pulse.db import get_db\nfrom src.pulse.services import (\n    ServiceCreate,\n    ServiceResponse,\n    create_service,\n    get_service,\n    list_services,\n)\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/api\", tags=[\"api\"])\n\n\n@router.get(\"/services\", response_model=list[ServiceResponse])\nasync def api_list_services():\n    async with get_db() as db:\n        return await list_services(db)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/services\", response_model=ServiceResponse, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)\nasync def api_create_service(service_in: ServiceCreate):\n    async with get_db() as db:\n        try:\n            new_service = await create_service(db, service_in)\n            return new_service\n        except ValueError as err:\n            raise HTTPException(\n                status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,\n                detail=str(err),\n            )\n\n\n@router.get(\"/services/{service_id}\", response_model=ServiceResponse)\nasync def api_get_service(service_id: int):\n    async with get_db() as db:\n        service = await get_service(db, service_id)\n        if not service:\n            raise HTTPException(\n                status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND,\n                detail=f\"Service with id {service_id} not found\",\n            )\n        return service\n","Overwrite":true,"Path":"D:/5 sem/ackopulse/src/pulse/api/routes.py"}:

create_service, list_services, ServiceCreate\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_01\nasync def test_t1_1_app_starts_health_ok(async_client: AsyncClient):\n    \"\"\"T1-1: App starts, /health returns ok.\"\"\"\n    resp = await async_client.get(\"/health\")\n    assert resp.status_code == 200\n    assert resp.json() == {\"status\": \"ok\"}\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_01\nasync def test_t1_2_tables_created_on_empty_db(initialized_db):\n    \"\"\"T1-2: Tables created on empty DB.\"\"\"\n    async with aiosqlite.connect(str(initialized_db)) as db:\n        async with db.execute(\"SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'\") as cursor:\n            tables = [row[0] for row in await cursor.fetchall()]\n    assert \"services\" in tables\n    assert \"health_checks\" in tables\n    assert \"incidents\" in tables\n    assert \"incident_events\" in tables\n    assert \"webhook_deliveries\" in tables\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_01\nasync def test_t1_3_restart_keeps_data(initialized_db):\n    \"\"\"T1-3: Reconnecting to existing DB retains persisted rows.\"\"\"\n    async with aiosqlite.connect(str(initialized_db)) as db:\n        await db.execute(\n            \"\"\"\n            INSERT INTO services (name, slug, health_url, owner, created_at)\n            VALUES ('Persist Svc', 'persist-svc', 'http://localhost:9001/health', 'dev@acko.com', '2026-11-18T00:00:00Z')\n            \"\"\"\n        )\n        await db.commit()\n\n    # Reconnect and verify data exists\n    async with aiosqlite.connect(str(initialized_db)) as db:\n        async with db.execute(\"SELECT name FROM services WHERE slug='persist-svc'\") as cursor:\n            row = await cursor.fetchone()\n            assert row is not None\n            assert row[0] == \"Persist Svc\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_01\nasync def test_t1_4_seed_inserts_exactly_4_and_idempotent(initialized_db):\n    \"\"\"T1-4: Seed inserts exactly 4; twice still 4.\"\"\"\n    await seed_services()\n    async with aiosqlite.connect(str(initialized_db)) as db:\n        async with db.execute(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM services\") as cursor:\n            count = (await cursor.fetchone())[0]\n            assert count == 4\n\n    # Run seed second time\n    await seed_services()\n    async with aiosqlite.connect(str(initialized_db)) as db:\n        async with db.execute(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM services\") as cursor:\n            count = (await cursor.fetchone())[0]\n            assert count == 4\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_01\nasync def test_t1_5_seeded_health_urls_match_starter_kit(initialized_db):\n    \"\"\"T1-5: Seeded health URLs match STARTER_KIT.md services and ports.\"\"\"\n    await seed_services()\n    async with aiosqlite.connect(str(initialized_db)) as db:\n        db.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row\n        async with db.execute(\"SELECT slug, health_url FROM services\") as cursor:\n            rows = {row[\"slug\"]: row[\"health_url\"] for row in await cursor.fetchall()}\n\n    assert \"quotes\" in rows and \"7001\" in rows[\"quotes\"]\n    assert \"payments\" in rows and \"7002\" in rows[\"payments\"]\n    assert \"claims\" in rows and \"7003\" in rows[\"claims\"]\n    assert \"notifications\" in rows and \"7004\" in rows[\"notifications\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_01\nasync def test_t1_6_list_returns_all(seeded_db, async_client: AsyncClient):\n    \"\"\"T1-6: GET /api/services returns all registered services.\"\"\"\n    resp = await async_client.get(\"/api/services\")\n    assert resp.status_code == 200\n    services = resp.json()\n    assert len(services) == 4\n    slugs = [s[\"slug\"] for s in services]\n    assert \"quotes\" in slugs\n    assert \"payments\" in slugs\n    assert \"claims\" in slugs\n    assert \"notifications\" in slugs\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_01\nasync def test_t1_7_valid_registration_appears_in_list(seeded_db, async_client: AsyncClient):\n    \"\"\"T1-7: POST /api/services registers service and appears in GET /api/services.\"\"\"\n    payload = {\n        \"name\": \"Auth Service\",\n        \"slug\": \"auth-service\",\n        \"health_url\": \"http://localhost:7005/health\",\n        \"owner\": \"auth-team@acko.com\",\n        \"interval_seconds\": 15,\n        \"slo_target\": 99.95,\n    }\n    resp = await async_client.post(\"/api/services\", json=payload)\n    assert resp.status_code == 201\n    created = resp.json()\n    assert created[\"name\"] == \"Auth Service\"\n    assert created[\"current_state\"] == \"HEALTHY\"\n\n    # Verify present in list\n    list_resp = await async_client.get(\"/api/services\")\n    names = [s[\"name\"] for s in list_resp.json()]\n    assert \"Auth Service\" in names\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_01\nasync def test_t1_8_invalid_registration_rejected(seeded_db, async_client: AsyncClient):\n    \"\"\"T1-8: Invalid URL, missing fields, out of bounds, duplicate rejected with 4xx.\"\"\"\n    # 1. Invalid URL scheme\n    bad_url = {\n        \"name\": \"Bad URL Service\",\n        \"health_url\": \"ftp://localhost:7000/health\",\n        \"owner\": \"dev@acko.com\",\n    }\n    r1 = await async_client.post(\"/api/services\", json=bad_url)\n    assert r1.status_code in (400, 422)\n\n    # 2. Missing required field (name)\n    missing_name = {\n        \"health_url\": \"http://localhost:7006/health\",\n        \"owner\": \"dev@acko.com\",\n    }\n    r2 = await async_client.post(\"/api/services\", json=missing_name)\n    assert r2.status_code == 422\n\n    # 3. Interval out of bounds (\u003c 1)\n    bad_interval = {\n        \"name\": \"Bad Interval\",\n        \"health_url\": \"http://localhost:7007/health\",\n        \"owner\": \"dev@acko.com\",\n        \"interval_seconds\": 0,\n    }\n    r3 = await async_client.post(\"/api/services\", json=bad_interval)\n    assert r3.status_code == 422\n\n    # 4. Duplicate name/health_url\n    duplicate = {\n        \"name\": \"Quotes Service\",  # already exists from seed\n        \"health_url\": \"http://localhost:7999/health\",\n        \"owner\": \"dev@acko.com\",\n    }\n    r4 = await async_client.post(\"/api/services\", json=duplicate)\n    assert r4.status_code == 400\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_01\nasync def test_t1_9_schema_has_required_columns(initialized_db):\n    \"\"\"T1-9: Schema has counter, state, next_check_at, first-failure columns.\"\"\"\n    async with aiosqlite.connect(str(initialized_db)) as db:\n        async with db.execute(\"PRAGMA table_info(services)\") as cursor:\n            cols = [row[1] for row in await cursor.fetchall()]\n\n    expected_cols = [\n        \"id\", \"name\", \"slug\", \"health_url\", \"owner\", \"interval_seconds\",\n        \"slo_target\", \"enabled\", \"current_state\", \"consecutive_failures\",\n        \"consecutive_successes\", \"first_failure_at\", \"next_check_at\", \"created_at\"\n    ]\n    for col in expected_cols:\n        assert col in cols, f\"Missing column {col} in services table\"\n","Overwrite":true,"Path":"D:/5 sem/ackopulse/tests/unit/test_unit_01_db_services.py"}:

> 
> The following required items are not currently covered in `DECISIONS.md`. Per the rules, implementation is stopped to present options:
> 
> #### 1. Failed-Check Definition
> - **Option A:** Any non-2xx status code (e.g., 4xx, 5xx), connection timeout, connection refusal, or DNS resolution failure constitutes a failed check.
>   - *Minutes:* 5 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Tests assert status codes 4xx/5xx persist code with error state; timeouts/refusals persist null status code with error message.
> - **Option B:** Only 5xx status codes, timeouts, and network connection errors count as failed checks; 3xx/4xx are classified as degraded.
>   - *Minutes:* 8 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Requires distinct test fixtures differentiating 4xx and 5xx assertions in `test_unit_02`.
> - **Option C:** Only explicit connection errors (timeouts, network drop, 503 Service Unavailable) count as failed; other non-2xx are classified as healthy with warning.
>   - *Minutes:* 10 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Requires testing non-standard classification table across multiple HTTP codes.
> 
> #### 2. `next_check_at` Update Rule & Stall / Catch-up Prevention
> - **Option A:** `next_check_at = clock.now() + timedelta(seconds=interval_seconds)` computed at probe completion.
>   - *Minutes:* 5 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Simple, strictly prevents catch-up bursts after stall because next check is anchored to current time. Tested by setting clock far into future and asserting exactly 1 check occurs.
> - **Option B:** `next_check_at = scheduled_at + timedelta(seconds=interval_seconds)`, but capped to `max(scheduled_at + interval, clock.now())` if overdue by more than one interval.
>   - *Minutes:* 8 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Tests must verify scheduling cadence preserves phase alignment when on time, but snaps to `now` upon stall.
> - **Option C:** Fixed cadence intervals calculated from initial start time with missed intervals discarded.
>   - *Minutes:* 12 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Requires state tracking of base timestamp and modulo interval testing.
> 
> #### 3. Overlap Handling & Skipped Runs Counter
> - **Option A:** In-memory `set[int]` of in-flight `service_id`s with an in-memory atomic integer counter `skipped_runs` exposed via checker stats.
>   - *Minutes:* 5 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Fast in-process unit tests verify when check takes longer than tick, service is skipped and `skipped_runs` increments by 1.
> - **Option B:** Database flag `is_running INTEGER` on `services` table and a `checker_stats` table in SQLite recording skip count.
>   - *Minutes:* 10 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Requires adding column migration/schema handling and testing DB transactions when crashes leave flag dirty.
> - **Option C:** Skip probe without tracking counter.
>   - *Minutes:* 3 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Does not fulfill product metric requirement to show how checking itself performs.
> 
> #### 4. DB Write Path for Checks
> - **Option A:** Immediate single transaction per completed check probe: insert row into `health_checks`, update `services.next_check_at`, commit immediately.
>   - *Minutes:* 5 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Fast checks persist results immediately before slow checks finish (verifying concurrency test T2-2).
> - **Option B:** Batch write: gather all concurrent probe results in a tick and write in one bulk transaction.
>   - *Minutes:* 8 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Fast checks would be delayed until the slowest check in the batch finishes, failing criterion T2-2.
> 
> #### 5. Clock Injection Policy
> - **Option A:** Central `src.pulse.clock.clock` injected into scheduler, probe, and services; tests advance clock via `clock.advance()` or `clock.set_time()`.
>   - *Minutes:* 5 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Fully deterministic tests with zero `asyncio.sleep` delays needed for interval testing.
> - **Option B:** Pass `clock: Clock` as explicit parameter to every prober/scheduler function call.
>   - *Minutes:* 8 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Requires parameter plumbing through all function signatures and routes.

> - **Option B:** `next_check_at = scheduled_at + timedelta(seconds=interval_seconds)`, but capped to `max(scheduled_at + interval, clock.now())` if overdue by more than one interval.
>   - *Minutes:* 8 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Tests must verify scheduling cadence preserves phase alignment when on time, but snaps to `now` upon stall.
> - **Option C:** Fixed cadence intervals calculated from initial start time with missed intervals discarded.
>   - *Minutes:* 12 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Requires state tracking of base timestamp and modulo interval testing.
> 
> #### 3. Overlap Handling & Skipped Runs Counter
> - **Option A:** In-memory `set[int]` of in-flight `service_id`s with an in-memory atomic integer counter `skipped_runs` exposed via checker stats.
>   - *Minutes:* 5 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Fast in-process unit tests verify when check takes longer than tick, service is skipped and `skipped_runs` increments by 1.
> - **Option B:** Database flag `is_running INTEGER` on `services` table and a `checker_stats` table in SQLite recording skip count.
>   - *Minutes:* 10 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Requires adding column migration/schema handling and testing DB transactions when crashes leave flag dirty.
> - **Option C:** Skip probe without tracking counter.
>   - *Minutes:* 3 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Does not fulfill product metric requirement to show how checking itself performs.
> 
> #### 4. DB Write Path for Checks
> - **Option A:** Immediate single transaction per completed check probe: insert row into `health_checks`, update `services.next_check_at`, commit immediately.
>   - *Minutes:* 5 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Fast checks persist results immediately before slow checks finish (verifying concurrency test T2-2).
> - **Option B:** Batch write: gather all concurrent probe results in a tick and write in one bulk transaction.
>   - *Minutes:* 8 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Fast checks would be delayed until the slowest check in the batch finishes, failing criterion T2-2.
> 
> #### 5. Clock Injection Policy
> - **Option A:** Central `src.pulse.clock.clock` injected into scheduler, probe, and services; tests advance clock via `clock.advance()` or `clock.set_time()`.
>   - *Minutes:* 5 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Fully deterministic tests with zero `asyncio.sleep` delays needed for interval testing.
> - **Option B:** Pass `clock: Clock` as explicit parameter to every prober/scheduler function call.
>   - *Minutes:* 8 min.
>   - *Test impact:* Requires parameter plumbing through all function signatures and routes.Z

> State classifier tests (test-first).\n\nPure classification and transitions without I/O.\nTests all 12 test-first requirements and transition table rows.\n\"\"\"\nimport pytest\nfrom src.pulse.state.classify import (\n    Outcome,\n    ServiceState,\n    Transition,\n    classify_raw_probe,\n    observe,\n)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_03\ndef test_1_fast_successful_response():\n    \"\"\"1. Fast successful response: 2xx and \u003c 1500ms from HEALTHY stays HEALTHY.\"\"\"\n    res = observe(\n        current_state=ServiceState.HEALTHY,\n        consecutive_failures=0,\n        consecutive_successes=1,\n        outcome=Outcome.FAST_OK,\n    )\n    assert res.new_state == ServiceState.HEALTHY\n    assert res.consecutive_successes == 2\n    assert res.consecutive_failures == 0\n    assert res.incident_action is None\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_03\ndef test_2_slow_successful_response():\n    \"\"\"2. Slow successful response: 2xx and \u003e= 1500ms transitions HEALTHY to DEGRADED.\"\"\"\n    res = observe(\n        current_state=ServiceState.HEALTHY,\n        consecutive_failures=0,\n        consecutive_successes=5,\n        outcome=Outcome.SLOW_OK,\n    )\n    assert res.new_state == ServiceState.DEGRADED\n    assert res.consecutive_failures == 0\n    assert res.consecutive_successes == 0\n    assert res.incident_action is None\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_03\ndef test_3_first_consecutive_failed_check():\n    \"\"\"3. First failed check from HEALTHY transitions to DEGRADED without opening incident.\"\"\"\n    res = observe(\n        current_state=ServiceState.HEALTHY,\n        consecutive_failures=0,\n        consecutive_successes=3,\n        outcome=Outcome.FAILED,\n    )\n    assert res.new_state == ServiceState.DEGRADED\n    assert res.consecutive_failures == 1\n    assert res.consecutive_successes == 0\n    assert res.incident_action is None\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_03\ndef test_4_failure_threshold_reached_opens_incident():\n    \"\"\"4. Reaching failure threshold (2 consecutive failures) transitions to DOWN and opens incident.\"\"\"\n    res = observe(\n        current_state=ServiceState.DEGRADED,\n        consecutive_failures=1,\n        consecutive_successes=0,\n        outcome=Outcome.FAILED,\n        failures_to_down=2,\n    )\n    assert res.new_state == ServiceState.DOWN\n    assert res.consecutive_failures == 2\n    assert res.consecutive_successes == 0\n    assert res.incident_action == \"open\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_03\ndef test_5_recovery_threshold_not_yet_reached():\n    \"\"\"5. First FAST_OK while DOWN transitions to intermediate DEGRADED, incident remains active.\"\"\"\n    res = observe(\n        current_state=ServiceState.DOWN,\n        consecutive_failures=3,\n        consecutive_successes=0,\n        outcome=Outcome.FAST_OK,\n        recovery_successes=2,\n    )\n    assert res.new_state == ServiceState.DEGRADED\n    assert res.consecutive_successes == 1\n    assert res.consecutive_failures == 0\n    assert res.incident_action is None\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_03\ndef test_6_recovery_threshold_reached_resolves_incident():\n    \"\"\"6. Second FAST_OK reaches recovery threshold (2), transitions to HEALTHY and resolves incident.\"\"\"\n    res = observe(\n        current_state=ServiceState.DEGRADED,\n        consecutive_failures=0,\n        consecutive_successes=1,\n        outcome=Outcome.FAST_OK,\n        recovery_successes=2,\n    )\n    assert res.new_state == ServiceState.HEALTHY\n    assert res.consecutive_successes == 2\n    assert res.consecutive_failures == 0\n    assert res.incident_action == \"resolve\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_03\ndef test_7_counter_resets():\n    \"\"\"7. Counter reset: failure resets successes to 0; SLOW_OK resets failures to 0.\"\"\"\n    # Failure resets successes\n    r1 = observe(\n        current_state=ServiceState.HEALTHY,\n        consecutive_failures=0,\n        consecutive_successes=5,\n        outcome=Outcome.FAILED,\n    )\n    assert r1.consecutive_successes == 0\n    assert r1.consecutive_failures == 1\n\n    # SLOW_OK resets failures to 0 per D-16\n    r2 = observe(\n        current_state=ServiceState.DEGRADED,\n        consecutive_failures=1,\n        consecutive_successes=0,\n        outcome=Outcome.SLOW_OK,\n    )\n    assert r2.consecutive_failures == 0\n    assert r2.consecutive_successes == 0\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_03\ndef test_8_all_permitted_transitions():\n    \"\"\"8. Verifies permitted transitions in transition table.\"\"\"\n    # HEALTHY -\u003e DEGRADED via SLOW_OK\n    assert observe(ServiceState.HEALTHY, 0, 0, Outcome.SLOW_OK).new_state == ServiceState.DEGRADED\n    # HEALTHY -\u003e DEGRADED via FAILED (first failure)\n    assert observe(ServiceState.HEALTHY, 0, 0, Outcome.FAILED).new_state == ServiceState.DEGRADED\n    # DEGRADED -\u003e DOWN via 2nd FAILED\n    assert observe(ServiceState.DEGRADED, 1, 0, Outcome.FAILED, failures_to_down=2).new_state == ServiceState.DOWN\n    # DOWN -\u003e DEGRADED via 1st FAST_OK\n    assert observe(ServiceState.DOWN, 2, 0, Outcome.FAST_OK, recovery_successes=2).new_state == ServiceState.DEGRADED\n    # DEGRADED -\u003e HEALTHY via 2nd FAST_OK\n    assert observe(ServiceState.DEGRADED, 0, 1, Outcome.FAST_OK, recovery_successes=2).new_state == ServiceState.HEALTHY\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_03\ndef test_9_boundary_conditions_at_exact_thresholds():\n    \"\"\"9. Exact boundary values for latency and thresholds.\"\"\"\n    # Latency boundary: 1499ms is FAST_OK, 1500ms is SLOW_OK\n    assert classify_raw_probe(200, 1499, None) == Outcome.FAST_OK\n    assert classify_raw_probe(200, 1500, None) == Outcome.SLOW_OK\n\n    # Failures boundary: failure 1 is DEGRADED, failure 2 is DOWN\n    assert observe(ServiceState.HEALTHY, 0, 0, Outcome.FAILED, failures_to_down=2).new_state == ServiceState.DEGRADED\n    assert observe(ServiceState.DEGRADED, 1, 0, Outcome.FAILED, failures_to_down=2).new_state == ServiceState.DOWN\n\n    # Recovery boundary: 1 success stays DEGRADED, 2 successes resolves to HEALTHY\n    assert observe(ServiceState.DOWN, 2, 0, Outcome.FAST_OK, recovery_successes=2).new_state == ServiceState.DEGRADED\n    assert observe(ServiceState.DEGRADED, 0, 1, Outcome.FAST_OK, recovery_successes=2).new_state == ServiceState.HEALTHY\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_03\ndef test_10_skipped_checks_do_not_affect_counters():\n    \"\"\"10. Skipped check leaves state and counters untouched.\"\"\"\n    res = observe(\n        current_state=ServiceState.DEGRADED,\n        consecutive_failures=1,\n        consecutive_successes=0,\n        outcome=Outcome.SKIP,\n    )\n    assert res.new_state == ServiceState.DEGRADED\n    assert res.consecutive_failures == 1\n    assert res.consecutive_successes == 0\n    assert res.incident_action is None\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_03\ndef test_11_initial_service_state():\n    \"\"\"11. Initial service state defaults to HEALTHY with 0/0 counters.\"\"\"\n    res = observe(\n        current_state=None,\n        consecutive_failures=0,\n        consecutive_successes=0,\n        outcome=Outcome.FAST_OK,\n    )\n    assert res.new_state == ServiceState.HEALTHY\n    assert res.consecutive_failures == 0\n    assert res.consecutive_successes == 1\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_03\ndef test_12_repeated_classifications_are_deterministic():\n    \"\"\"12. Pure function: repeated classifications produce identical, consistent transitions.\"\"\"\n    t1 = observe(ServiceState.HEALTHY, 0, 2, Outcome.FAST_OK)\n    t2 = observe(ServiceState.HEALTHY, 0, 2, Outcome.FAST_OK)\n    assert t1 == t2\n","Overwrite":true,"Path":"D:/5 sem/ackopulse/tests/unit/test_unit_03_state_classifier.py"}:

> ({"Content":"\"\"\"Incident management: persistence, one-active guard, events, ack, notes.\n\nFollows DECISIONS.md D-02, D-03, D-09, D-11.\n\"\"\"\nfrom src.pulse.clock import clock\n\n\nasync def open_incident(db, service_id: int, service_name: str, now_iso: str | None = None) -\u003e int | None:\n    \"\"\"Opens one active incident for the service if none is currently active.\"\"\"\n    now_ts = now_iso or clock.now().isoformat()\n    # Guard against duplicate active incidents\n    async with db.execute(\n        \"SELECT id FROM incidents WHERE service_id = ? AND status = 'active'\",\n        (service_id,),\n    ) as cursor:\n        existing = await cursor.fetchone()\n        if existing:\n            return existing[0]\n\n    title = f\"Service {service_name} is DOWN\"\n    cursor = await db.execute(\n        \"\"\"\n        INSERT INTO incidents (service_id, opened_at, status, title)\n        VALUES (?, ?, 'active', ?)\n        \"\"\",\n        (service_id, now_ts, title),\n    )\n    incident_id = cursor.lastrowid\n    await db.execute(\n        \"\"\"\n        INSERT INTO incident_events (incident_id, event_type, message, created_at)\n        VALUES (?, 'opened', ?, ?)\n        \"\"\",\n        (incident_id, f\"Incident opened: {title}\", now_ts),\n    )\n    return incident_id\n\n\nasync def resolve_incident(db, service_id: int, now_iso: str | None = None) -\u003e int | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolves active incident for the service if one exists.\"\"\"\n    now_ts = now_iso or clock.now().isoformat()\n    async with db.execute(\n        \"SELECT id FROM incidents WHERE service_id = ? AND status = 'active'\",\n        (service_id,),\n    ) as cursor:\n        row = await cursor.fetchone()\n        if not row:\n            return None\n        incident_id = row[0]\n\n    await db.execute(\n        \"UPDATE incidents SET status = 'resolved', resolved_at = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n        (now_ts, incident_id),\n    )\n    await db.execute(\n        \"\"\"\n        INSERT INTO incident_events (incident_id, event_type, message, created_at)\n        VALUES (?, 'resolved', 'Service recovered to HEALTHY', ?)\n        \"\"\",\n        (incident_id, now_ts),\n    )\n    return incident_id\n\n\nasync def acknowledge_incident(\n    db, incident_id: int, acknowledged_by: str = \"operator\", now_iso: str | None = None\n) -\u003e dict:\n    \"\"\"Acknowledges an active incident idempotently. Rejects if resolved.\"\"\"\n    now_ts = now_iso or clock.now().isoformat()\n    async with db.execute(\n        \"SELECT id, service_id, status, acknowledged_at, acknowledged_by FROM incidents WHERE id = ?\",\n        (incident_id,),\n    ) as cursor:\n        row = await cursor.fetchone()\n        if not row:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Incident {incident_id} not found\")\n\n        status, ack_at = row[2], row[3]\n        if status == \"resolved\":\n            raise ValueError(\"Cannot acknowledge a resolved incident\")\n\n        # Idempotent: if already acknowledged, do not insert duplicate event\n        if ack_at:\n            return {\"id\": incident_id, \"acknowledged\": True, \"acknowledged_at\": ack_at}\n\n    await db.execute(\n        \"UPDATE incidents SET acknowledged_at = ?, acknowledged_by = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n        (now_ts, acknowledged_by, incident_id),\n    )\n    await db.execute(\n        \"\"\"\n        INSERT INTO incident_events (incident_id, event_type, message, created_at)\n        VALUES (?, 'acknowledged', ?, ?)\n        \"\"\",\n        (incident_id, f\"Acknowledged by {acknowledged_by}\", now_ts),\n    )\n    await db.commit()\n    return {\"id\": incident_id, \"acknowledged\": True, \"acknowledged_at\": now_ts}\n\n\nasync def add_incident_note(\n    db, incident_id: int, note: str, now_iso: str | None = None\n) -\u003e dict:\n    \"\"\"Appends an operator note to the incident event timeline.\"\"\"\n    note = note.strip()\n    if not note:\n        raise ValueError(\"Note cannot be empty\")\n\n    now_ts = now_iso or clock.now().isoformat()\n    async with db.execute(\n        \"SELECT id, status FROM incidents WHERE id = ?\", (incident_id,)\n    ) as cursor:\n        row = await cursor.fetchone()\n        if not row:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Incident {incident_id} not found\")\n\n    await db.execute(\n        \"\"\"\n        INSERT INTO incident_events (incident_id, event_type, message, created_at)\n        VALUES (?, 'note_added', ?, ?)\n        \"\"\",\n        (incident_id, note, now_ts),\n    )\n    await db.commit()\n    return {\"incident_id\": incident_id, \"note\": note, \"created_at\": now_ts}\n\n\nasync def get_incident_timeline(db, incident_id: int) -\u003e list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Returns chronological events for an incident.\"\"\"\n    async with db.execute(\n        \"\"\"\n        SELECT id, incident_id, event_type, message, created_at\n        FROM incident_events\n        WHERE incident_id = ?\n        ORDER BY id ASC\n        \"\"\",\n        (incident_id,),\n    ) as cursor:\n        rows = await cursor.fetchall()\n        return [dict(r) for r in rows]\n","Overwrite":true,"Path":"D:/5 sem/ackopulse/src/pulse/state/incidents.py"}:

> 3{"Content":"\"\"\"Scheduler: select due services, run concurrently, persist each result\nin one immediate transaction (D-14), update next_check_at = now + interval\n(D-12), skip in-flight services and count skips (D-13), apply state classification\nand incident lifecycle (D-01, D-02, D-03, D-16, D-17).\"\"\"\nimport asyncio\nfrom datetime import timedelta\n\nimport aiosqlite\nimport httpx\n\nfrom src.pulse.checker.probe import probe\nfrom src.pulse.clock import clock\nfrom src.pulse.config import settings\nfrom src.pulse.state.classify import (\n    ServiceState,\n    classify_raw_probe,\n    observe,\n)\nfrom src.pulse.state.incidents import open_incident, resolve_incident\n\nDUE_SQL = (\n    \"SELECT id, name, health_url, interval_seconds FROM services \"\n    \"WHERE enabled = 1 AND next_check_at IS NOT NULL \"\n    \"AND next_check_at \u003c= ?\"\n)\n\n\nclass Scheduler:\n    def __init__(self, max_concurrency: int = 10):\n        self.in_flight: set[int] = set()\n        self.skipped_runs: int = 0\n        self._sem = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)\n        self._client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None\n\n    async def run_once(self, db: aiosqlite.Connection) -\u003e int:\n        \"\"\"One tick: check all due services concurrently. Returns run count.\"\"\"\n        now = clock.now().isoformat()\n        async with db.execute(DUE_SQL, (now,)) as cur:\n            rows = await cur.fetchall()\n        due = [\n            {\"id\": r[0], \"name\": r[1], \"health_url\": r[2], \"interval_seconds\": r[3]}\n            for r in rows\n        ]\n\n        runnable = []\n        for svc in due:\n            if svc[\"id\"] in self.in_flight:\n                self.skipped_runs += 1  # D-13\n            else:\n                runnable.append(svc)\n\n        if runnable:\n            if self._client is None:\n                self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=settings.check_timeout_seconds)\n            results = await asyncio.gather(  # exceptions never kill the tick\n                *(self._probe_one(s) for s in runnable), return_exceptions=True\n            )\n            for r in results:\n                if isinstance(r, Exception):\n                    pass  # counted; one failing check must not stop others\n        return len(runnable)\n\n    async def _probe_one(self, svc: dict) -\u003e None:\n        async with self._sem:\n            self.in_flight.add(svc[\"id\"])\n            try:\n                result = await probe(svc, client=self._client)  # D-08 timeout on shared client\n                await self._persist(svc, result)  # immediate write, D-14\n            except Exception:\n                pass  # one failing check must not stop others\n            finally:\n                self.in_flight.discard(svc[\"id\"])\n\n    async def _persist(self, svc: dict, result) -\u003e None:\n        # Classify raw probe\n        outcome = classify_raw_probe(\n            http_status=result.http_status,\n            latency_ms=result.latency_ms,\n            error=result.error_message,\n            degraded_threshold_ms=settings.degraded_latency_threshold_ms,\n        )\n        check_state = outcome.value\n        next_check = (clock.now() + timedelta(seconds=svc[\"interval_seconds\"])).isoformat()  # D-12\n        now_ts = clock.now().isoformat()\n\n        async with aiosqlite.connect(str(settings.db_path)) as db:  # D-14: one immediate txn\n            db.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row\n\n            # 1. Fetch current service state and counters\n            async with db.execute(\n                \"\"\"SELECT current_state, consecutive_failures, consecutive_successes, first_failure_at\n                   FROM services WHERE id = ?\"\"\",\n                (svc[\"id\"],),\n            ) as cur:\n                s_row = await cur.fetchone()\n\n            curr_state = s_row[\"current_state\"] if s_row else \"HEALTHY\"\n            fails = s_row[\"consecutive_failures\"] if s_row else 0\n            succs = s_row[\"consecutive_successes\"] if s_row else 0\n            first_fail = s_row[\"first_failure_at\"] if s_row else None\n\n            # 2. Compute state transition\n            transition = observe(\n                current_state=curr_state,\n                consecutive_failures=fails,\n                consecutive_successes=succs,\n                outcome=outcome,\n                failures_to_down=settings.failures_to_down,\n                recovery_successes=settings.recovery_successes,\n            )\n\n            # 3. Handle first_failure_at tracking\n            if transition.consecutive_failures == 1 and not first_fail:\n                first_fail = result.checked_at\n            elif transition.new_state == ServiceState.HEALTHY:\n                first_fail = None\n\n            # 4. Insert health_checks row (raw observation)\n            await db.execute(\n                \"\"\"INSERT INTO health_checks\n                   (service_id, scheduled_at, started_at, checked_at, duration_ms,\n                    http_status, latency_ms, state, error_message)\n                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\"\"\",\n                (\n                    result.service_id,\n                    result.scheduled_at,\n                    result.started_at,\n                    result.checked_at,\n                    result.duration_ms,\n                    result.http_status,\n                    result.latency_ms,\n                    check_state,\n                    result.error_message,\n                ),\n            )\n\n            # 5. Update service with derived state and counters\n            await db.execute(\n                \"\"\"UPDATE services\n                   SET next_check_at = ?, current_state = ?,\n                       consecutive_failures = ?, consecutive_successes = ?,\n                       first_failure_at = ?\n                   WHERE id = ?\"\"\",\n                (\n                    next_check,\n                    transition.new_state.value,\n                    transition.consecutive_failures,\n                    transition.consecutive_successes,\n                    first_fail,\n                    svc[\"id\"],\n                ),\n            )\n\n            # 6. Apply incident lifecycle\n            if transition.incident_action == \"open\":\n                await open_incident(db, svc[\"id\"], svc[\"name\"], now_ts)\n            elif transition.incident_action == \"resolve\":\n                await resolve_incident(db, svc[\"id\"], now_ts)\n\n            await db.commit()\n","Overwrite":true,"Path":"D:/5 sem/ackopulse/src/pulse/checker/scheduler.py"}:

Verify active incident created\n        inc_cur = await db.execute(\n            \"SELECT id, status, title FROM incidents WHERE service_id = ? AND status = 'active'\",\n            (sid,),\n        )\n        inc = await inc_cur.fetchone()\n        assert inc is not None\n        assert inc[\"status\"] == \"active\"\n\n        # Check 3: Another failure does NOT create a duplicate active incident\n        await set_due(db, sid)\n        await sched.run_once(db)\n\n        all_inc_cur = await db.execute(\n            \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incidents WHERE service_id = ? AND status = 'active'\",\n            (sid,),\n        )\n        assert (await all_inc_cur.fetchone())[0] == 1\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_03\nasync def test_15_recovery_resolves_incident(initialized_db, fake_server):\n    \"\"\"DB integration: 2 healthy checks resolves active incident and returns state to HEALTHY.\"\"\"\n    async with aiosqlite.connect(initialized_db) as db:\n        # Start in down mode with 2 failures\n        sid = await add_service(db, \"s-rec\", f\"{fake_server}/error500\")\n        sched = Scheduler()\n\n        await set_due(db, sid)\n        await sched.run_once(db)\n        await set_due(db, sid)\n        await sched.run_once(db)\n\n        # Now change health_url to healthy endpoint\n        await db.execute(\"UPDATE services SET health_url = ? WHERE id = ?\", (f\"{fake_server}/ok\", sid))\n        await db.commit()\n\n        # Check 1: Intermediate recovery (DEGRADED, incident still active)\n        await set_due(db, sid)\n        await sched.run_once(db)\n        db.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row\n        s_row = await (await db.execute(\"SELECT current_state FROM services WHERE id = ?\", (sid,))).fetchone()\n        assert s_row[\"current_state\"] == \"DEGRADED\"\n\n        # Check 2: Full recovery (HEALTHY, incident resolved)\n        await set_due(db, sid)\n        await sched.run_once(db)\n        s_row2 = await (await db.execute(\"SELECT current_state FROM services WHERE id = ?\", (sid,))).fetchone()\n        assert s_row2[\"current_state\"] == \"HEALTHY\"\n\n        # Incident status is resolved\n        inc_row = await (await db.execute(\"SELECT status, resolved_at FROM incidents WHERE service_id = ?\", (sid,))).fetchone()\n        assert inc_row[\"status\"] == \"resolved\"\n        assert inc_row[\"resolved_at\"] is not None\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit_03\nasync def test_16_acknowledge_and_notes(initialized_db, fake_server):\n    \"\"\"Incident acknowledge and notes lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    from src.pulse.state.incidents import acknowledge_incident, add_incident_note, get_incident_timeline\n    async with aiosqlite.connect(initialized_db) as db:\n        sid = await add_service(db, \"s-ack\", f\"{fake_server}/error500\")\n        sched = Scheduler()\n        await set_due(db, sid)\n        await sched.run_once(db)\n        await set_due(db, sid)\n        await sched.run_once(db)\n\n        # Get active incident\n        cur = await db.execute(\"SELECT id FROM incidents WHERE service_id = ?\", (sid,))\n        inc_id = (await cur.fetchone())[0]\n\n        # Acknowledge\n        ack_res = await acknowledge_incident(db, inc_id, acknowledged_by=\"alice\")\n        assert ack_res[\"acknowledged\"] is True\n\n        # Add Note\n        await add_incident_note(db, inc_id, \"Investigating database cluster timeout.\")\n\n        # Check timeline\n        timeline = await get_incident_timeline(db, inc_id)\n        event_types = [e[\"event_type\"] for e in timeline]\n        assert event_types == [\"opened\", \"acknowledged\", \"note_added\"]\n\n        # Resolve incident\n        await db.execute(\"UPDATE incidents SET status = 'resolved' WHERE id = ?\", (inc_id,))\n        await db.commit()\n\n        # Acknowledging resolved incident should fail\n        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=\"Cannot acknowledge a resolved incident\"):\n            await acknowledge_incident(db, inc_id)\n","Path":"D:/5 sem/ackopulse/tests/unit/test_unit_03_state_classifier.py"}:

await open_incident(db, p_id, p_name, now_iso=\"2026-11-18T10:00:00Z\")\n        # Claims: resolved incident\n        c_inc = await open_incident(db, c_id, c_name, now_iso=\"2026-11-18T09:00:00Z\")\n
