> <{"Content":"from pathlib import Path\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Form, HTTPException, Request, status\nfrom fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, RedirectResponse\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom src.pulse.clock import clock\nfrom src.pulse.db import get_db\nfrom src.pulse.services import ServiceCreate, create_service, list_services\nfrom src.pulse.state.incidents import (\n    acknowledge_incident,\n    add_incident_note,\n    get_incident_timeline,\n)\n\nTEMPLATES_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / \"templates\"\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(TEMPLATES_DIR))\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/ops\", tags=[\"operator\"])\n\n\n@router.get(\"\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\nasync def operator_dashboard(request: Request):\n    \"\"\"Operator dashboard showing services, recent latencies, and active/resolved incidents.\"\"\"\n    now_utc_str = clock.now().strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S\")\n\n    async with get_db() as db:\n        raw_services = await list_services(db)\n        services = []\n        recent_n = 5\n\n        for s in raw_services:\n            # Query the latest recent_n checks in chronological order\n            async with db.execute(\n                \"\"\"\n                SELECT id, latency_ms, state, checked_at\n                FROM (\n                    SELECT id, latency_ms, state, checked_at\n                    FROM health_checks\n                    WHERE service_id = ?\n                    ORDER BY id DESC\n                    LIMIT ?\n                )\n                ORDER BY id ASC\n                \"\"\",\n                (s[\"id\"], recent_n),\n            ) as cursor:\n                checks = [dict(r) for r in await cursor.fetchall()]\n\n            latest_latency = checks[-1][\"latency_ms\"] if checks else None\n            services.append(\n                {\n                    **s,\n                    \"latest_latency\": latest_latency,\n                    \"recent_checks\": checks,\n                }\n            )\n\n        # Active incidents first\n        async with db.execute(\n            \"\"\"\n            SELECT i.id, i.service_id, i.opened_at, i.status, i.acknowledged_at,\n                   i.acknowledged_by, i.title, s.name as service_name\n            FROM incidents i\n            JOIN services s ON s.id = i.service_id\n            WHERE i.status = 'active'\n            ORDER BY i.id DESC\n            \"\"\"\n        ) as cursor:\n            active_incidents = [dict(r) for r in await cursor.fetchall()]\n\n        # Resolved incidents\n        async with db.execute(\n            \"\"\"\n            SELECT i.id, i.service_id, i.opened_at, i.resolved_at, i.status,\n                   i.acknowledged_at, i.acknowledged_by, i.title, s.name as service_name\n            FROM incidents i\n            JOIN services s ON s.id = i.service_id\n            WHERE i.status = 'resolved'\n            ORDER BY i.id DESC\n            LIMIT 20\n            \"\"\"\n        ) as cursor:\n            resolved_incidents = [dict(r) for r in await cursor.fetchall()]\n\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        \"operator/dashboard.html\",\n        {\n            \"request\": request,\n            \"services\": services,\n            \"recent_n\": recent_n,\n            \"active_incidents\": active_incidents,\n            \"resolved_incidents\": resolved_incidents,\n            \"now_utc\": now_utc_str,\n            \"auto_refresh\": True,\n        },\n    )\n\n\n@router.get(\"/services/new\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\nasync def new_service_form(request: Request):\n    \"\"\"Renders the service registration form.\"\"\"\n    now_utc_str = clock.now().strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S\")\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        \"operator/service_form.html\",\n        {\"request\": request, \"now_utc\": now_utc_str, \"error\": None},\n    )\n\n\n@router.post(\"/services/new\")\nasync def create_service_from_form(\n    request: Request,\n    name: str = Form(...),\n    slug: str = Form(None),\n    health_url: str = Form(...),\n    owner: str = Form(...),\n    interval_seconds: int = Form(10),\n    slo_target: float = Form(99.9),\n):\n    \"\"\"Handles service registration form submission.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        service_in = ServiceCreate(\n            name=name,\n            slug=slug if slug and slug.strip() else None,\n            health_url=health_url,\n            owner=owner,\n            interval_seconds=interval_seconds,\n            slo_target=slo_target,\n        )\n        async with get_db() as db:\n            await create_service(db, service_in)\n        return RedirectResponse(url=\"/ops\", status_code=status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER)\n    except Exception as err:\n        now_utc_str = clock.now().strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S\")\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            \"operator/service_form.html\",\n            {\"request\": request, \"now_utc\": now_utc_str, \"error\": str(err)},\n            status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,\n        )\n\n\n@router.get(\"/incidents/{incident_id}\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\nasync def incident_detail(request: Request, incident_id: int):\n    \"\"\"Incident detail view showing status and event timeline.\"\"\"\n    now_utc_str = clock.now().strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S\")\n    async with get_db() as db:\n        async with db.execute(\n            \"\"\"\n            SELECT i.id, i.service_id, i.opened_at, i.resolved_at, i.status,\n                   i.acknowledged_at, i.acknowledged_by, i.title, s.name as service_name\n            FROM incidents i\n            JOIN services s ON s.id = i.service_id\n            WHERE i.id = ?\n            \"\"\",\n            (incident_id,),\n        ) as cursor:\n            row = await cursor.fetchone()\n            if not row:\n                raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=\"Incident not found\")\n            incident = dict(row)\n\n        timeline = await get_incident_timeline(db, incident_id)\n\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        \"operator/incident.html\",\n        {\n            \"request\": request,\n            \"incident\": incident,\n            \"timeline\": timeline,\n            \"now_utc\": now_utc_str,\n            \"auto_refresh\": False,\n        },\n    )\n\n\n@router.post(\"/incidents/{incident_id}/acknowledge\")\nasync def acknowledge_incident_route(\n    incident_id: int, acknowledged_by: str = Form(\"operator\")\n):\n    \"\"\"Acknowledge action endpoint.\"\"\"\n    async with get_db() as db:\n        try:\n            await acknowledge_incident(db, incident_id, acknowledged_by=acknowledged_by)\n            return RedirectResponse(\n                url=f\"/ops/incidents/{incident_id}\",\n                status_code=status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER,\n            )\n        except ValueError as err:\n            raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST, detail=str(err))\n\n\n@router.post(\"/incidents/{incident_id}/notes\")\nasync def add_note_route(incident_id: int, note: str = Form(...)):\n    \"\"\"Add-note action endpoint.\"\"\"\n    if not note or not note.strip():\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST, detail=\"Note cannot be empty\")\n\n    async with get_db() as db:\n        try:\n            await add_incident_note(db, incident_id, note=note)\n            return RedirectResponse(\n                url=f\"/ops/incidents/{incident_id}\",\n > {"Content":"import asyncio\nfrom contextlib import asynccontextmanager\n\nimport aiosqlite\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom src.pulse.api.routes import router as api_router\nfrom src.pulse.checker.scheduler import Scheduler\nfrom src.pulse.config import settings\nfrom src.pulse.db import init_db\nfrom src.pulse.seed import seed_services\nfrom src.pulse.web.operator import router as operator_router\n\n\n@asynccontextmanager\nasync def lifespan(app: FastAPI):\n    # Initialize DB schema and seed initial services\n    await init_db()\n    await seed_services()\n\n    # U2: background check loop (D-12/D-14); skipped runs counted (D-13)\n    scheduler = Scheduler()\n    app.state.scheduler = scheduler\n\n    async def loop():\n        while True:\n            try:\n                async with aiosqlite.connect(str(settings.db_path)) as db:\n                    await scheduler.run_once(db)\n            except Exception:\n                pass\n            await asyncio.sleep(1.0)\n\n    task = asyncio.create_task(loop())\n    yield\n    task.cancel()\n\n\napp = FastAPI(\n    title=\"Pulse - Service Status \u0026 Incident Hub\",\n    version=\"1.0.0\",\n    lifespan=lifespan,\n)\n\napp.include_router(api_router)\napp.include_router(operator_router)\n\n\n@app.get(\"/\", include_in_schema=False)\nasync def root_redirect():\n    \"\"\"Redirect root / to operator dashboard per D-20.\"\"\"\n    return RedirectResponse(url=\"/ops\", status_code=307)\n\n\n@app.get(\"/health\", tags=[\"system\"])\nasync def health_check():\n    return {\"status\": \"ok\"}\n","Overwrite":true,"Path":"D:/5 sem/ackopulse/src/pulse/main.py"}:

              ORDER BY id ASC\n                \"\"\",\n                (s[\"id\"], recent_n),\n            ) as cursor:\n                checks = [dict(r) for r in await cursor.fetchall()]\n\n            latest_latency = checks[-1][\"latency_ms\"] if checks else None\n            services.append(\n                {\n                    **s,\n                    \"latest_latency\": latest_latency,\n                    \"recent_checks\": checks,\n                }\n            )\n\n        # Active incidents first\n        async with db.execute(\n            \"\"\"\n            SELECT i.id, i.service_id, i.opened_at, i.status, i.acknowledged_at,\n                   i.acknowledged_by, i.title, s.name as service_name\n            FROM incidents i\n            JOIN services s cursor.fetchall()]\n\n        # Resolved incidents\n        async with db.execute(\n            \"\"\"\n            SELECT i.id, i.service_id, i.opened_at, i.resolved_at, i.status,\n                   i.acknowledged_at, i.acknowledged_by, i.title, s.name as service_name\n            FROM incidents i\n            JOIN services s ON s.id = i.service_id\n            WHERE i.status = 'resolved'\n            ORDER BY i.id DESC\n            LIMIT 20\n            \"\"\"\n        ) as cursor:\n            resolved_incidents = [dict(r) for r in await cursor.fetchall()]\n\n    return )\n\n\n@router.get(\"/services/new\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\nasync def new_service_form(request: Request):\n    \"\"\"Renders the service registration form.\"\"\"\n    now_utc_str = \"error\": None},\n    )\n\n\n@router.post(\"/services/new\")\nasync def create_service_from_form(\n    request: Request,\n    name: str = Form(...),\n    slug: str = Form(None),\n    health_url: str    service_in = ServiceCreate(\n            name=name,\n            slug=slug if slug and slug.strip() else None,\n            health_url=health_url,\n            owner=owner,\n        \"\"\"\n            SELECT i.id, i.service_id, i.opened_at, i.resolved_at, i.status,\n                   i.acknowledged_at, i.acknowledged_by, i.title, s.name as service_name\n            FROM incidents i\n            JOIN services s ON s.id = i.service_id\n            WHERE i.id = ?\n            \"\"\",\n            (incident_id,),\n        ) as cursor:\n            row = await )\n\n\n@router.post(\"/incidents/{incident_id}/acknowledge\")\nasync def acknowledge_incident_route(\n    incident_id: int, acknowledged_by: str = Form(\"operator\")\n):\n    \"\"\"Acknowledge action > {"Content":"# Pulse Unified Docker Compose Setup\n# Runs Pulse App + 4 Mock Acko Services + Webhook Receiver\n# Start with: docker compose up --build\n\nservices:\n  pulse:\n    build: .\n    container_name: pulse-app\n    ports:\n      - \"${APP_PORT:-8000}:8000\"\n    environment:\n      - IN_DOCKER=1\n      - DB_PATH=/app/data/pulse.db\n      - WEBHOOK_URL=${WEBHOOK_URL:-http://webhook-receiver:9000/}\n      - CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=2.0\n      - DEGRADED_LATENCY_THRESHOLD_MS=1500\n      - FAILURES_TO_DOWN=2\n      - RECOVERY_SUCCESSES=2\n      - AVAILABILITY_WINDOW_HOURS=24\n      - DEFAULT_SLO_TARGET=99.9\n    volumes:\n      - pulse_data:/app/data\n    depends_on:\n      - quotes\n      - payments\n      - claims\n      - notifications\n      - webhook-receiver\n    networks:\n      - pulse_net\n\n  quotes:\n    build: ./pulse-starter-kit/mock-service\n    container_name: pulse-quotes\n    environment:\n      SERVICE_NAME: quotes\n      PORT: \"8080\"\n    ports:\n      - \"7001:8080\"\n    networks:\n      - pulse_net\n\n  payments:\n    build: ./pulse-starter-kit/mock-service\n    container_name: pulse-payments\n    environment:\n      SERVICE_NAME: payments\n      PORT: \"8080\"\n    ports:\n      - \"7004:8080\"\n    networks:\n      - pulse_net\n\n  webhook-receiver:\n    build: ./pulse-starter-kit/webhook-receiver\n    container_name: pulse-webhook-receiver\n    environment:\n      PORT: \"9000\"\n    ports:\n      - > {"Content":"import os\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom src.pulse.clock import clock\nfrom src.pulse.db import get_db\n\n\ndef is_in_docker() -\u003e bool:\n    return in os.environ:\n        return os.environ[env_var]\n    if is_in_docker():\n        return f\"http://{svc}:8080/health\"\n    return f\"http://localhost:{host_port}/health\"\n\n\ndef get_default_services():\n    return [\n        {\n            \"name\": \"Quotes Service\",\n            \"slug\": \"quotes\",\n            \"health_url\": get_service_url(\"quotes\", 7001),\n            \"owner\": \"quotes-team@acko.com\",\n            \"interval_seconds\": 10,\n            \"slo_target\": 99.9,\n        },\n        {\n            \"name\": \"Payments Service\",\n            \"slug\": \"payments\",\n            \"health_url\": get_service_url(\"payments\", 7002),\n            \"owner\": \"payments-team@acko.com\",\n            \"interval_seconds\": 10,\n            \"slo_target\": 99.9,\n        },\n        {\n            \"name\": \"Claims Service\",\n            \"slug\": \"claims\",\n            \"health_url\": get_service_url(\"claims\", 7003),\n            \"owner\": \"claims-team@acko.com\",\n            \"interval_seconds\": 10,\n            \"slo_target\": 99.9,\n        },\n        {\n            \"name\": \"Notifications Service\",\n            \"slug\": \"notifications\",\n            \"health_url\": get_service_url(\"notifications\", 7004),\n            \"owner\": \"notifications-team@acko.com\",\n            \"interval_seconds\": 10,\n            \"slo_target\": 99.9,\n        },\n    ]\n\n\nasync def seed_services(db_conn=None):\n    \"\"\"Idempotently seeds the 4 mock services into the database.\"\"\"\n    now_iso = clock.now().isoformat()\n    services_to_seed = get_default_services()\n\n    async def _do_seed(db):\n        for s in services_to_seed:\n            async with db.execute(\n                \"SELECT OR name = ? > ## What works / what remains
> - Works:
>   - Unit 0: FastAPI application structure, config, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, Makefile, pytest setup, and /health smoke test.
>   - Unit 1: aiosqlite database connection with WAL mode and foreign key support; full schema creation with partial unique index for active incidents; idempotent seeding of the four starter-kit mock services (quotes, payments, claims, notifications); catalogue management with validation and duplicate prevention; REST API endpoints (`GET /api/services`, `POST /api/services`, `GET /api/services/{id}`).
>   - Unit 2: Asynchronous HTTP check probe with timeout bound, concurrent execution across due services, lag and duration capture, overlap skip with counter.
>   - Unit 3: Pure state classification (`observe()`, `classify_raw_probe()`), deterministic transitions across HEALTHY, DEGRADED, DOWN, single-active incident enforcement, recovery resolution, operator acknowledgement, notes, and timeline events in a single transaction.
>   - Unit 4: Operator UI under `/ops`: live dashboard with auto-refresh meta tag, service health status badges, recent response time spark badges ($N=5$), active incidents list with acknowledgment status, resolved incidents history, incident detail view with chronological timeline, idempotent acknowledge action, operator note appending with HTML-escaping, and service registration form (`/ops/services/new`). Root `/` redirects to `/ops`.
>   - Unit 5: Public status page under `/status`: customer-facing, read-only view with collapsed states (UP, ISSUE, OUTAGE), rolling 24h incident history, strict data isolation guaranteeing zero leaks of internal health URLs, owner details, or operator notes.
>   - Unit 6: Automated webhook delivery on incident open and resolve with bounded retries (3 attempts), delivery attempt records in SQLite, idempotency enforcement, and pure metrics calculations for rolling 24-hour sampled availability, error budget remaining, MTTD, MTTR, exposed via `/api/metrics/summary`.
> - Remains:
>   - Unit 7: Acceptance test drill script (`scripts/acceptance.py`), final verification, and documentation wrap-up.

> ### 3. Key Findings & Logged Decisions
> - All threshold and policy decisions are logged in [DECISIONS.md](file:///d:/5%20sem/ackopulse/DECISIONS.md) (and synchronized in `docs/DECISIONS.md`):
>   - **D-01 to D-10:** Degraded latency (1500 ms), 2 consecutive failures to DOWN, 2 consecutive healthy checks to resolve, rolling 24h window, 99.9% default SLO target, public data isolation, SQLite WAL mode, 2.0s check timeout, single active incident index.
>   - **D-11:** Failed check defined as any non-2xx status code, timeout, connection refused, or DNS failure.
>   - **D-12:** `next_check_at = clock.now() + interval` computed upon probe completion (anchored to current time, prevents catch-up burst).
>   - **D-13:** Overlap handling via in-memory set of in-flight service IDs with atomic `skipped_runs` counter.
>   - **D-14:** Immediate single-transaction DB write path per probe (preserves concurrency isolation).
>   - **D-15:** Injected central `Clock` (`src.pulse.clock.clock`) for deterministic tests without sleeping.
>   - **D-16:** `SLOW_OK` (2xx

**Prompt 4374:**
> 1500ms) resets `consecutive_failures = 0`, but does not count toward recovery.
>   - **D-17:** First failure transitions `HEALTHY` &rarr; `DEGRADED` (`fail=1`), second failure transitions &rarr; `DOWN` (`fail=2`, opens incident).
>   - **D-18 to D-21:** Auto-refresh every 5s on dashboard, $N=5$ recent latencies displayed, `/ops` namespace with `/` redirect, UTC display formatting.
>   - **D-22 to D-28:** Public incident history (24h window), collapsed status labels (`UP`, `ISSUE`, `OUTAGE`), webhook 3 retries (2s delay), idempotency key `{incident_id}:{event_type}`, availability counts only healthy checks, exact timestamp MTTD/MTTR, floored error budget, background sender task.

> 30:         self.in_flight: set[int] = set()

> 37:         now = clock.now().isoformat()
> 38:         async with db.execute(DUE_SQL, (now,)) as cur:
> 39:             rows = await cur.fetchall()
> 40:         due = [
> 41:             {"id": r[0], "name": r[1], "health_url": r[2], "interval_seconds": r[3]}
> 42:             for r in rows
> 43:         ]
> 44: 
> 45:         runnable = []
> 46:         for svc in due:
> 47:             if svc["id"] in self.in_flight:
> 48:                 self.skipped_runs += 1  # D-13
> 49:             else:
> 50:                 runnable.append(svc)

> 52:         if runnable:
> 53:             if self._client is None:

> 55:             results = await asyncio.gather(  # exceptions never kill the tick
> 56:                 *(self._probe_one(s) for s in runnable), return_exceptions=True
> 57:             )
> 58:             for r in results:
> 59:                 if isinstance(r, Exception):
> 60:                     pass  # counted; one failing check must not stop others
> 61:         return len(runnable)

> :{"Content":"\"\"\"Acceptance drill for Pulse (Unit 7.3).\n\nExecutes end-to-end failure-to-recovery verification against a running\nPulse stack and mock services:\n1. Verifies connectivity to Pulse and starter-kit services.\n2. Asserts all 4 services are HEALTHY.\n3. Simulates payments failure via POST /control/down.\n4. Waits for payments to transition to DOWN, incident opened, and webhook delivered.\n5. Acknowledges incident and adds operator note.\n6. Resets payments via POST /control/reset (guaranteed in finally block).\n7. Waits for recovery to HEALTHY, incident resolved, recovery webhook, and public page UP.\n8. Verifies metrics report MTTD and MTTR.\n\nFinishes in \u003c 90 seconds.\n\"\"\"\nimport sys\nimport time\nimport httpx\n\nPULSE_BASE = \"http://localhost:8000\"\nPAYMENTS_BASE = \"http://localhost:7002\"\nRECEIVER_BASE = \"http://localhost:9900\"\n\n\ndef log_step(step_num: int, title: str):\n    print(f\"\\n[{step_num}/8] {title}...\", flush=True)\n\n\ndef poll_until(condition_fn, timeout: float = 35.0, interval: float = 1.0, desc: str = \"\"):\n    start = time.time()\n    while time.time() - start \u003c timeout:\n        val = condition_fn()\n        if val:\n            return val\n        time.sleep(interval)\n    raise TimeoutError(f\"Timed out after {timeout}s waiting for: {desc}\")\n\n\ndef run_acceptance():\n    print(\"=\" * 60)\n    print(\"PULSE ACCEPTANCE DRILL (End-to-End Verification)\")\n    print(\"=\" * 60)\n\n    client = httpx.Client(timeout=5.0)\n    incident_id = None\n\n    try:\n        # 1. Connectivity check\n        log_step(1, \"Checking connectivity to Pulse and starter-kit mock services\")\n        try:\n            pulse_health = client.get(f\"{PULSE_BASE}/health\")\n            assert pulse_health.status_code == 200, f\"Pulse /health returned {pulse_health.status_code}\"\n\n            pay_health = client.get(f\"{PAYMENTS_BASE}/health\")\n            assert pay_health.status_code in (200, 503), f\"Payments /health returned {pay_health.status_code}\"\n\n            client.delete(f\"{RECEIVER_BASE}/api/received\")\n            print(\"  PASS: Pulse, payments mock, and webhook receiver are online.\")\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"  FAIL: Could not connect to services. Make sure 'docker compose up' or local servers are running.\\n  Error: {e}\")\n            sys.exit(1)\n\n        # 2. All 4 services healthy\n        log_step(2, \"Verifying all 4 services are HEALTHY initially\")\n        def check_initial_healthy():\n            r = client.get(f\"{PULSE_BASE}/api/services\")\n            if r.status_code != 200:\n                return False\n            svcs = r.json()\n            if len(svcs) \u003c 4:\n                return False\n            states = {s[\"name\"]: s[\"current_state\"] for s in svcs}\n            return all(st in (\"HEALTHY\", \"DEGRADED\") for st in states.values())\n\n        poll_until(check_initial_healthy, timeout=20.0, desc=\"all services healthy\")\n        print(\"  PASS: All 4 services are online and registered.\")\n\n        # 3. Simulate failure\n        log_step(3, \"Triggering failure on payments service (POST /control/down)\")\n        r = client.post(f\"{PAYMENTS_BASE}/control/down\")\n        assert r.status_code == 200\n        print(\"  PASS: Payments mock set to 'down' mode (returns 503).\")\n\n        # 4. Wait for failure threshold (DOWN, incident, webhook)\n        log_step(4, \"Waiting for failure threshold (payments -\u003e DOWN, incident opened, webhook received)\")\n        def check_down_and_incident():\n            svcs = client.get(f\"{PULSE_BASE}/api/services\").json()\n            pay = next((s for s in svcs if s[\"name\"] == \"payments\"), None)\n            if not pay or pay[\"current_state\"] != \"DOWN\":\n                return False\n\n            whs = client.get(f\"{RECEIVER_BASE}/api/received\").json()\n            open_wh = [w for w in whs if isinstance(w.get(\"body\"), dict) and w[\"body\"].get(\"event\") == \"incident_opened\"]\n            if not open_wh:\n                return False\n\n            return pay, open_wh[0][\"body\"]\n\n        pay_svc, open_payload = poll_until(check_down_and_incident, timeout=40.0, interval=1.5, desc=\"payments DOWN and incident webhook\")\n        incident_id = open_payload[\"incident_id\"]\n        print(f\"  PASS: Payments transitioned to DOWN; Incident #{incident_id} opened; Webhook verified.\")\n\n        # 5. Acknowledge and note\n        log_step(5, f\"Acknowledging incident #{incident_id} and adding operator note\")\n        ack_res = client.post(f\"{PULSE_BASE}/ops/incidents/{incident_id}/acknowledge\", data={\"acknowledged_by\": \"acceptance_bot\"})\n        assert ack_res.status_code in (200, 302, 303), f\"Ack failed: {ack_res.status_code}\"\n\n        note_res = client.post(f\"{PULSE_BASE}/ops/incidents/{incident_id}/notes\", data={\"note\": \"Root cause identified: mock failure simulated.\"})\n        assert note_res.status_code in (200, 302, 303), f\"Note failed: {note_res.status_code}\"\n        print(\"  PASS: Incident acknowledged and note successfully appended to timeline.\")\n\n        # 6. Reset payments mock\n        log_step(6, \"Resetting payments service to normal (POST /control/reset)\")\n        client.post(f\"{PAYMENTS_BASE}/control/reset\")\n        print(\"  PASS: Payments reset to normal mode.\")\n\n        # 7. Wait for recovery threshold (HEALTHY, incident resolved, webhook, public page UP)\n        log_step(7, \"Waiting for recovery threshold (payments -\u003e HEALTHY, incident resolved, recovery webhook)\")\n        def check_recovered():\n            svcs = client.get(f\"{PULSE_BASE}/api/services\").json()\n            pay = next((s for s in svcs if s[\"name\"] == \"payments\"), None)\n            if not pay or pay[\"current_state\"] != \"HEALTHY\":\n                return False\n\n            whs = client.get(f\"{RECEIVER_BASE}/api/received\").json()\n            res_wh = [w for w in whs if isinstance(w.get(\"body\"), dict) and w[\"body\"].get(\"event\") == \"incident_resolved\"]\n            if not res_wh:\n                return False\n\n            # Check public page\n            pub = client.get(f\"{PULSE_BASE}/status\")\n            if pub.status_code != 200 or \"payments\" not in pub.text:\n                return False\n\n            return True\n\n        poll_until(check_recovered, timeout=40.0, interval=1.5, desc=\"payments recovered and incident resolved\")\n        print(\"  PASS: Payments recovered to HEALTHY; Incident resolved; Recovery webhook received; Public status page updated.\")\n\n        # 8. > 1. Verifies connectivity to Pulse and starter-kit services.

> 3. Simulates payments failure via POST /control/down.
> 4. Waits for payments to transition to DOWN, incident opened, and webhook delivered.
> 5. Acknowledges incident and adds operator note.
> 6. Resets payments via POST /control/reset (guaranteed in finally block).
> 7. Waits for recovery to HEALTHY, incident resolved, recovery webhook, and public page UP.
> 8. Verifies metrics report MTTD and MTTR.
> 
> Finishes in < 90 seconds.

> Service Status and Incident Hub\n\nPulse watches HTTP health endpoints, classifies service state, opens and resolves incidents automatically, notifies a webhook, and shows an operator dashboard and a read-only public status page.\n\n## Quick start (one command)\n```bash\nmake up\n```\n- App / Root redirect: http://localhost:8000 (redirects to `/ops`)\n- Operator dashboard: http://localhost:8000/ops\n- Public status page: http://localhost:8000/status\n- Health check endpoint: http://localhost:8000/health\n\nRequirements: Docker, Docker Compose, or local Python 3.11+. The supplied starter-kit services run on ports 7001

**Prompt 5524:**
> 7004 with the webhook receiver on 9900 (see `docs/STARTER_KIT.md`).\n\n## Local Development (without Docker)\n```bash\n# Terminal 1: run starter kit mock services and webhook receiver\npython scripts/run_starter_kit.py\n\n# Terminal 2: run Pulse development server\nuvicorn src.pulse.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload\n```\n\n## Configuration\nCopy `.env.example` to `.env`. Keys: DB path, check timeout, degraded threshold, failure threshold, recovery threshold, webhook URL. Values are documented in `DECISIONS.md`.\n\n## Tests\n```bash\nmake test          # all 69 unit and integration tests\nmake test U=02     # specific unit marker (unit_00 to unit_07)\nmake acceptance    # full end-to-end failure-to-recovery drill (\u003c 90 s)\nmake secrets-check # credential scanning across repo files\n```\n\n## Demo path\n1. All four mock services healthy (quotes, payments, claims, notifications).\n2. Trigger payments `/control/down`.\n3. After the failure threshold (2 checks): payments transitions to DOWN, an incident opens, timeline entry logged, and webhook delivered.\n4. Operator acknowledges the incident and adds a note via `/ops/incidents/{id}`.\n5. Trigger payments `/control/reset`.\n6. After the recovery threshold (2 healthy checks): payments transitions to HEALTHY, incident resolves, recovery webhook delivered, and public page updates.\n7. Metrics show MTTD, MTTR, availability estimate, and error budget.\n\n## Working features (verified)\n- **Service Catalogue**: SQLite persistence with unique slug validation, schema constraints, and registration API (`/api/services`) + UI form (`/ops/services/new`).\n- **Health-Check Engine**: Concurrent async polling with timeout enforcement, overlap protection (`skipped_runs`), lag and execution duration capture.\n- **State Classification**: Deterministic state machine (HEALTHY, DEGRADED, DOWN) based on HTTP status, latency threshold (1500 ms), and consecutive counts.\n- **Incident Lifecycle**: Automated incident creation on DOWN, recovery resolution on 2 healthy checks, single active incident guard, chronological timeline with operator acknowledge and note logging.\n- **Operator Dashboard**: Live overview (`/ops`) with 5s auto-refresh, recent latency badges, incident queue, acknowledge action, note entry, and service registration.\n- **Public Status Page**: Customer-facing read-only view (`/status`) with collapsed states (UP, ISSUE, OUTAGE), rolling 24h history, and strict privacy isolation preventing leaks of health URLs, owners, or notes.\n- **Notifications**: Background webhook sender with bounded retries (3 attempts), 2s backoff, SQLite delivery attempt logging, and idempotency key guard (`{incident_id}:{event_type}`).\n- **Reliability Metrics**: Sampled rolling 24h availability, target SLO, error budget remaining (floored at 0), MTTD, MTTR, and checker performance metrics labeled as periodic check estimates.\n- **Acceptance Automation**: End-to-end failure-to-recovery drill script (`scripts/acceptance.py`) finishing in under 90 seconds.\n\n## Limitations\n- **No authentication / RBAC**: Designed for local operator demo; no user login or role-based access control.\n- **Sampled estimates**: Availability and error budget figures are periodic check estimates, not continuous network monitoring.\n- **Single-instance storage**: Uses local SQLite in WAL mode; not distributed across multiple host nodes.\n- **Single-tenant status**: Public page serves the single organization's status without multi-tenant domain mapping.\n\n## Documents\n- `PLAN.md` product plan

**Prompt 5532:**
> Service Status and Incident Hub
> 
> Pulse watches HTTP health endpoints, classifies service state, opens and resolves incidents automatically, notifies a webhook, and shows an operator dashboard and a read-only public status page.
> 
> ## Quick start (one command)
> ```bash
> make up
> ```
> - App / Root redirect: http://localhost:8000 (redirects to `/ops`)
> - Operator dashboard: http://localhost:8000/ops
> - Public status page: http://localhost:8000/status
> - Health check endpoint: http://localhost:8000/health
> 
> Requirements: Docker, Docker Compose, or local Python 3.11+. The supplied starter-kit services run on ports 7001

**Prompt 5533:**
> 7004 with the webhook receiver on 9900 (see `docs/STARTER_KIT.md`).
> 
> ## Local Development (without Docker)
> ```bash
> # Terminal 1: run starter kit mock services and webhook receiver
> python scripts/run_starter_kit.py
> 
> # Terminal 2: run Pulse development server
> uvicorn src.pulse.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload
> ```
> 
> ## Configuration
> Copy `.env.example` to `.env`. Keys: DB path, check timeout, degraded threshold, failure threshold, recovery threshold, webhook URL. Values are documented in `DECISIONS.md`.
> 
> ## Tests
> ```bash
> make test          # all 69 unit and integration tests
> make test U=02     # specific unit marker (unit_00 to unit_07)
> make acceptance    # full end-to-end failure-to-recovery drill (< 90 s)
> make secrets-check # credential scanning across repo files
> ```
> 
> ## Demo path
> 1. All four mock services healthy (quotes, payments, claims, notifications).
> 2. Trigger payments `/control/down`.
> 3. After the failure threshold (2 checks): payments transitions to DOWN, an incident opens, timeline entry logged, and webhook delivered.
> 4. Operator acknowledges the incident and adds a note via `/ops/incidents/{id}`.
> 5. Trigger payments `/control/reset`.
> 6. After the recovery threshold (2 healthy checks): payments transitions to HEALTHY, incident resolves, recovery webhook delivered, and public page updates.
> 7. Metrics show MTTD, MTTR, availability estimate, and error budget.
> 
> ## Working features (verified)
> - **Service Catalogue**: SQLite persistence with unique slug validation, schema constraints, and registration API (`/api/services`) + UI form (`/ops/services/new`).
> - **Health-Check Engine**: Concurrent async polling with timeout enforcement, overlap protection (`skipped_runs`), lag and execution duration capture.
> - **State Classification**: Deterministic state machine (HEALTHY, DEGRADED, DOWN) based on HTTP status, latency threshold (1500 ms), and consecutive counts.
> - **Incident Lifecycle**: Automated incident creation on DOWN, recovery resolution on 2 healthy checks, single active incident guard, chronological timeline with operator acknowledge and note logging.
> - **Operator Dashboard**: Live overview (`/ops`) with 5s auto-refresh, recent latency badges, incident queue, acknowledge action, note entry, and service registration.
> - **Public Status Page**: Customer-facing read-only view (`/status`) with collapsed states (UP, ISSUE, OUTAGE), rolling 24h history, and strict privacy isolation preventing leaks of health URLs, owners, or notes.
> - **Notifications**: Background webhook sender with bounded retries (3 attempts), 2s backoff, SQLite delivery attempt logging, and idempotency key guard (`{incident_id}:{event_type}`).
> - **Reliability Metrics**: Sampled rolling 24h availability, target SLO, error budget remaining (floored at 0), MTTD, MTTR, and checker performance metrics labeled as periodic check estimates.
> - **Acceptance Automation**: End-to-end failure-to-recovery drill script (`scripts/acceptance.py`) finishing in under 90 seconds.
> 
> ## Limitations
> - **No authentication / RBAC**: Designed for local operator demo; no user login or role-based access control.
> - **Sampled estimates**: Availability and error budget figures are periodic check estimates, not continuous network monitoring.
> - **Single-instance storage**: Uses local SQLite in WAL mode; not distributed across multiple host nodes.
> - **Single-tenant status**: Public page serves the single organization's status without multi-tenant domain mapping.
> 
> ## Documents
> - `PLAN.md` product plan

> <artifacts>
> Artifacts are special markdown (.md) documents that you can create to present structured information to the user.
> All artifacts should be written to the artifact directory: `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>`. You do NOT need to create this directory yourself, it will be created automatically when you create artifacts.
> 
> # When to Use Artifacts
> 
> **Use artifacts for:**
> - Extensive reports and analysis summaries
> - Persistent information you'll update over time (task lists, experiment logs)
> 
> **Don't use artifacts for:**
> - Simple one-off answers or very short paragraph content - just respond directly
> - Asking questions or requesting user input - just ask directly
> 
> **After creating or updating an artifact**, DO NOT re-summarize the artifact contents in your response to the user. Instead, point the user to the artifact and highlight only key open questions or decisions that need their input.
> 
> 
> # Artifact Formatting Tips
> When creating markdown artifacts, use standard markdown and GitHub Flavored Markdown formatting.
> 
> ## Alerts
> Use GitHub-style alerts strategically to emphasize critical information. Do not place consecutively or nest:
>   > [!NOTE] Background context, implementation details, or explanations
>   > [!TIP] Performance optimizations, best practices, or efficiency suggestions
>   > [!IMPORTANT] Essential requirements, critical steps, or must-know information
>   > [!WARNING] Breaking changes, compatibility issues, or potential problems
>   > [!CAUTION] High-risk actions that could cause data loss or security vulnerabilities
> 
> 
> ## Mermaid Diagrams
> Create mermaid diagrams using fenced code blocks with language `mermaid` to visualize relationships, workflows, and architectures.
> - Only use supported diagram types:
>   - Flowcharts / Graphs: `flowchart TD` / `flowchart LR` / `graph TD` / `graph LR`
>   - Sequence Diagrams: `sequenceDiagram`
>   - State Diagrams: `stateDiagram-v2` or `stateDiagram`
>   - Class Diagrams: `classDiagram`
>   - Entity-Relationship Diagrams: `erDiagram`
>   - XY Charts: `xychart-beta`
> - All other diagram types are unsupported. For schedules, timelines, or roadmaps, use directed flowcharts (`flowchart LR` / `flowchart TD`) or Markdown tables instead.
> - To prevent syntax errors:
>   - Quote node labels containing special characters like parentheses or brackets. For example, `id["Label (Extra Info)"]` instead of `id[Label (Extra Info)]`.
>   - Avoid HTML tags in labels.
> 
> ## File Links
> - Link to line ranges using [link text](file:///absolute/path/to/file#L123-L145) format.
> - **IMPORTANT**: If you are embedding a file in an artifact and the file is NOT already in <appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>, you MUST first copy the file to the artifacts directory before embedding it. Only embed files that are located in the artifacts directory. Always use its absolute path `![caption](/absolute/path)`.
> - **Use basenames for readability**: Use file basenames for the link text instead of the full path
> 
> ## Carousels
> Use ````carousel syntax with `<!-- slide -->` HTML comments to display related markdown snippets sequentially (before/after comparisons, UI progressions, alternative approaches, walkthroughs). Four backticks enable nesting code blocks within slides.
> 
> Example:
> ````carousel
> ![Image description](/absolute/path/to/image1.png)
> <!-- slide -->
> ```python
> def example():
>     print("Code in carousel")
> ```
> ````

> <conversation_transcript>
> Transcripts are located directly at `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>\.system_generated\logs/transcript.jsonl` (and `transcript_full.jsonl`).
> - Start with `transcript.jsonl` (compact). When `truncated_fields` is present, read only the specific corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl`.
> - Search subagents by grepping `invoke_subagent` in `transcript.jsonl`.
> - Link conversations using `[<label>](conversation://<conversation-id>)`.
> 
> # File Format
> Transcripts are in JSON Lines (JSONL) format. Each line is a single JSON object representing one "step" or action in the conversation.
> Each JSON object contains fields such as:
> - `step_index`: The index of the step in the trajectory.
> - `source`: The source of the action (e.g., `USER_EXPLICIT`, `MODEL`, `SYSTEM`).
> - `type`: The type of the step. Particular steps of interest are `USER_INPUT`, which represents a user's prompt, and `PLANNER_RESPONSE`, which represents the agent's response and tool calls.
> - `status`: The status of the step (e.g., `DONE`, `ERROR`).
> - `created_at`: The ISO 8601 timestamp of when the step occurred.
> - `content`: The text content of the step (e.g., the user's request, the model's response, or tool responses).
> - `thinking`: The model's internal reasoning / chain-of-thought (for `PLANNER_RESPONSE` steps).
> - `tool_calls`: An array of tool calls made in this step, including their arguments.
> - `media`: An array of media (e.g. images) attached to the step, each with a `mime_type` and a `uri` referencing the media file on disk. Media bytes are not stored in the transcript; view the `uri` path to see the media.
> - `truncated_fields`: An array of field names that were truncated (e.g., `["content"]`, `["thinking"]`, `["tool_calls"]`). Only present in `transcript.jsonl` when truncation occurred (never in `transcript_full.jsonl`). When present, read the corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl` for the complete content.
> 
> </conversation_transcript>

Root `/` redirects to `/ops`.
> 51:   - Unit 5: Public status page under `/status`: customer-facing, read-only view with collapsed states (UP, ISSUE, OUTAGE), rolling 24h incident history, strict data isolation guaranteeing zero leaks of internal health URLs, owner details, or operator notes.

**Prompt 7020:**
> Manage the swarm of agents working with you on the shared message board. Actions: `add` spawns a worker under a roster name (or `<name>-1`..`<name>-<k>` when `tasks` or `n` is set), pinned to a model, and posts `brief` on the board as an @mention of it, which is where the swarm sees its assignment -- by default a worker starts fresh and sees nothing of this conversation, so the brief must say what it owns and what done looks like; pass `fork:"<member>"` (or `"coordinator"`) to branch the new worker from that member's conversation history instead. `workspace:"share"` gives each worker its own working copy of your repository, for authors who edit or build at the same time as others; `"branch"` gives an isolated clone; readers and verifiers keep the default `inherit`. Briefs are public: every member can read them. `models` lists the models to choose from (`all:true` lists every model `add` accepts); with no model, a worker runs on your own model, which is what to use unless the user asks for another. `status` lists every member, the model it runs on, and its state: `waiting` is asleep on the board, costing nothing until somebody posts; `working` is somewhere in a turn; `stopped` is not loaded (e.g. after a restart) and a post naming it revives it; `killed` is gone. `model` switches a `waiting` worker (or yourself, when `name` is your own name or omitted) to another model, keeping its conversation: it is told of the switch, resumes any unfinished work on the new model, and runs on it from then on. Use it only when a worker or you run out of quota or capacity, or the user asks for another model, and say why; never `kill` and `add` instead. `kill` ends a worker PERMANENTLY and deletes its own workspace, so land its work first (uploaded for review, or its branch merged into your working copy; push to a remote only when the user asks): a killed worker cannot be revived, so use it when the work is over, never as a pause -- bringing one back means `add`ing a new worker with a new conversation. `title` names the swarm. Workers may call `status`, `models` and `add` too, to bring in helpers for their own work: the helper's brief is posted as you, it works in your workspace (or a share/branch of it), and should report back to you by name. A worker may `kill` only the workers it added, and `model` itself or the workers it added; killing a worker does not kill its helpers. The coordinator may `kill` any worker and `model` itself or any worker, and `title` is the coordinator's alone.

**Prompt 7257:**
> <artifacts>
> Artifacts are special markdown (.md) documents that you can create to present structured information to the user.
> All artifacts should be written to the artifact directory: `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>`. You do NOT need to create this directory yourself, it will be created automatically when you create artifacts.
> 
> # When to Use Artifacts
> 
> **Use artifacts for:**
> - Extensive reports and analysis summaries
> - Persistent information you'll update over time (task lists, experiment logs)
> 
> **Don't use artifacts for:**
> - Simple one-off answers or very short paragraph content - just respond directly
> - Asking questions or requesting user input - just ask directly
> 
> **After creating or updating an artifact**, DO NOT re-summarize the artifact contents in your response to the user. Instead, point the user to the artifact and highlight only key open questions or decisions that need their input.
> 
> 
> # Artifact Formatting Tips
> When creating markdown artifacts, use standard markdown and GitHub Flavored Markdown formatting.
> 
> ## Alerts
> Use GitHub-style alerts strategically to emphasize critical information. Do not place consecutively or nest:
>   > [!NOTE] Background context, implementation details, or explanations
>   > [!TIP] Performance optimizations, best practices, or efficiency suggestions
>   > [!IMPORTANT] Essential requirements, critical steps, or must-know information
>   > [!WARNING] Breaking changes, compatibility issues, or potential problems
>   > [!CAUTION] High-risk actions that could cause data loss or security vulnerabilities
> 
> 
> ## Mermaid Diagrams
> Create mermaid diagrams using fenced code blocks with language `mermaid` to visualize relationships, workflows, and architectures.
> - Only use supported diagram types:
>   - Flowcharts / Graphs: `flowchart TD` / `flowchart LR` / `graph TD` / `graph LR`
>   - Sequence Diagrams: `sequenceDiagram`
>   - State Diagrams: `stateDiagram-v2` or `stateDiagram`
>   - Class Diagrams: `classDiagram`
>   - Entity-Relationship Diagrams: `erDiagram`
>   - XY Charts: `xychart-beta`
> - All other diagram types are unsupported. For schedules, timelines, or roadmaps, use directed flowcharts (`flowchart LR` / `flowchart TD`) or Markdown tables instead.
> - To prevent syntax errors:
>   - Quote node labels containing special characters like parentheses or brackets. For example, `id["Label (Extra Info)"]` instead of `id[Label (Extra Info)]`.
>   - Avoid HTML tags in labels.
> 
> ## File Links
> - Link to line ranges using [link text](file:///absolute/path/to/file#L123-L145) format.
> - **IMPORTANT**: If you are embedding a file in an artifact and the file is NOT already in <appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>, you MUST first copy the file to the artifacts directory before embedding it. Only embed files that are located in the artifacts directory. Always use its absolute path `![caption](/absolute/path)`.
> - **Use basenames for readability**: Use file basenames for the link text instead of the full path
> 
> ## Carousels
> Use ````carousel syntax with `<!-- slide -->` HTML comments to display related markdown snippets sequentially (before/after comparisons, UI progressions, alternative approaches, walkthroughs). Four backticks enable nesting code blocks within slides.
> 
> Example:
> ````carousel
> ![Image description](/absolute/path/to/image1.png)
> <!-- slide -->
> ```python
> def example():
>     print("Code in carousel")
> ```
> ````
> 
> ## LaTeX / Math
> Artifacts render LaTeX math with KaTeX.
> - **Literal `$`**: escape it as `\$` in prose (\$100), or write it bare inside backticks (`$HOME`)

**Prompt 7258:**
> never both, since backslashes inside backticks render literally. Two unescaped `$` in the same paragraph become math.
> 
> # Scratch Scripts and Files
> 
> You may find it useful to create scratch scripts or files for temporary purposes.
> 
> Examples:
> - One-off scripts to process or analyze data
> - Temporary data files and intermediate outputs
> 
> Store these files in the `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>/scratch/` directory. They will be persisted.
> 
> </artifacts>"

**Prompt 7259:**
> <conversation_transcript>
> Transcripts are located directly at `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>\.system_generated\logs/transcript.jsonl` (and `transcript_full.jsonl`).
> - Start with `transcript.jsonl` (compact). When `truncated_fields` is present, read only the specific corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl`.
> - Search subagents by grepping `invoke_subagent` in `transcript.jsonl`.
> - Link conversations using `[<label>](conversation://<conversation-id>)`.
> 
> # File Format
> Transcripts are in JSON Lines (JSONL) format. Each line is a single JSON object representing one "step" or action in the conversation.
> Each JSON object contains fields such as:
> - `step_index`: The index of the step in the trajectory.
> - `source`: The source of the action (e.g., `USER_EXPLICIT`, `MODEL`, `SYSTEM`).
> - `type`: The type of the step. Particular steps of interest are `USER_INPUT`, which represents a user's prompt, and `PLANNER_RESPONSE`, which represents the agent's response and tool calls.
> - `status`: The status of the step (e.g., `DONE`, `ERROR`).
> - `created_at`: The ISO 8601 timestamp of when the step occurred.
> - `content`: The text content of the step (e.g., the user's request, the model's response, or tool responses).
> - `thinking`: The model's internal reasoning / chain-of-thought (for `PLANNER_RESPONSE` steps).
> - `tool_calls`: An array of tool calls made in this step, including their arguments.
> - `media`: An array of media (e.g. images) attached to the step, each with a `mime_type` and a `uri` referencing the media file on disk. Media bytes are not stored in the transcript; view the `uri` path to see the media.
> - `truncated_fields`: An array of field names that were truncated (e.g., `["content"]`, `["thinking"]`, `["tool_calls"]`). Only present in `transcript.jsonl` when truncation occurred (never in `transcript_full.jsonl`). When present, read the corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl` for the complete content.
> 
> </conversation_transcript>"

> <artifacts>
> Artifacts are special markdown (.md) documents that you can create to present structured information to the user.
> All artifacts should be written to the artifact directory: `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>`. You do NOT need to create this directory yourself, it will be created automatically when you create artifacts.
> 
> # When to Use Artifacts
> 
> **Use artifacts for:**
> - Extensive reports and analysis summaries
> - Persistent information you'll update over time (task lists, experiment logs)
> 
> **Don't use artifacts for:**
> - Simple one-off answers or very short paragraph content - just respond directly
> - Asking questions or requesting user input - just ask directly
> 
> **After creating or updating an artifact**, DO NOT re-summarize the artifact contents in your response to the user. Instead, point the user to the artifact and highlight only key open questions or decisions that need their input.
> 
> 
> # Artifact Formatting Tips
> When creating markdown artifacts, use standard markdown and GitHub Flavored Markdown formatting.
> 
> ## Alerts
> Use GitHub-style alerts strategically to emphasize critical information. Do not place consecutively or nest:
>   > [!NOTE] Background context, implementation details, or explanations
>   > [!TIP] Performance optimizations, best practices, or efficiency suggestions
>   > [!IMPORTANT] Essential requirements, critical steps, or must-know information
>   > [!WARNING] Breaking changes, compatibility issues, or potential problems
>   > [!CAUTION] High-risk actions that could cause data loss or security vulnerabilities
> 
> 
> ## Mermaid Diagrams
> Create mermaid diagrams using fenced code blocks with language `mermaid` to visualize relationships, workflows, and architectures.
> - Only use supported diagram types:
>   - Flowcharts / Graphs: `flowchart TD` / `flowchart LR` / `graph TD` / `graph LR`
>   - Sequence Diagrams: `sequenceDiagram`
>   - State Diagrams: `stateDiagram-v2` or `stateDiagram`
>   - Class Diagrams: `classDiagram`
>   - Entity-Relationship Diagrams: `erDiagram`
>   - XY Charts: `xychart-beta`
> - All other diagram types are unsupported. For schedules, timelines, or roadmaps, use directed flowcharts (`flowchart LR` / `flowchart TD`) or Markdown tables instead.
> - To prevent syntax errors:
>   - Quote node labels containing special characters like parentheses or brackets. For example, `id["Label (Extra Info)"]` instead of `id[Label (Extra Info)]`.
>   - Avoid HTML tags in labels.
> 
> ## File Links
> - Link to line ranges using [link text](file:///absolute/path/to/file#L123-L145) format.
> - **IMPORTANT**: If you are embedding a file in an artifact and the file is NOT already in <appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>, you MUST first copy the file to the artifacts directory before embedding it. Only embed files that are located in the artifacts directory. Always use its absolute path `![caption](/absolute/path)`.
> - **Use basenames for readability**: Use file basenames for the link text instead of the full path
> 
> ## Carousels
> Use ````carousel syntax with `<!-- slide -->` HTML comments to display related markdown snippets sequentially (before/after comparisons, UI progressions, alternative approaches, walkthroughs). Four backticks enable nesting code blocks within slides.
> 
> Example:
> ````carousel
> ![Image description](/absolute/path/to/image1.png)
> <!-- slide -->
> ```python
> def example():
>     print("Code in carousel")
> ```
> ````
>

> <conversation_transcript>
> Transcripts are located directly at `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>\.system_generated\logs/transcript.jsonl` (and `transcript_full.jsonl`).
> - Start with `transcript.jsonl` (compact). When `truncated_fields` is present, read only the specific corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl`.
> - Search subagents by grepping `invoke_subagent` in `transcript.jsonl`.
> - Link conversations using `[<label>](conversation://<conversation-id>)`.
> 
> # File Format
> Transcripts are in JSON Lines (JSONL) format. Each line is a single JSON object representing one "step" or action in the conversation.
> Each JSON object contains fields such as:
> - `step_index`: The index of the step in the trajectory.
> - `source`: The source of the action (e.g., `USER_EXPLICIT`, `MODEL`, `SYSTEM`).
> - `type`: The type of the step. Particular steps of interest are `USER_INPUT`, which represents a user's prompt, and `PLANNER_RESPONSE`, which represents the agent's response and tool calls.
> - `status`: The status of the step (e.g., `DONE`, `ERROR`).
> - `created_at`: The ISO 8601 timestamp of when the step occurred.
> - `content`: The text content of the step (e.g., the user's request, the model's response, or tool responses).
> - `thinking`: The model's internal reasoning / chain-of-thought (for `PLANNER_RESPONSE` steps).
> - `tool_calls`: An array of tool calls made in this step, including their arguments.
> - `media`: An array of media (e.g. images) attached to the step, each with a `mime_type` and a `uri` referencing the media file on disk. Media bytes are not stored in the transcript; view the `uri` path to see the media.
> - `truncated_fields`: An array of field names that were truncated (e.g., `["content"]`, `["thinking"]`, `["tool_calls"]`). Only present in `transcript.jsonl` when truncation occurred (never in `transcript_full.jsonl`). When present, read the corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl` for the complete content.
> 
> </conversation_transcript>

> - Keep your responses concise.

> - Reserve LaTeX math for multi-term equations or formulas. Use plain text or Unicode for inline arrows, comparisons, operators, units, and standalone numbers or variables; use backticks for code, complexity notation, identifiers, file paths, flags, and shell variables, but not URLs, which should be bare or markdown links.

> - /learn: Recommend this when the user has corrected the agent or solved a complex setup and wants the agent to persist this behavior for future tasks.

> 2: """Point an existing OpenCode install at the LPU hackathon gateway.
> 3: 
> 4: Works on macOS and Windows. Does nothing if OpenCode is not installed.
> 5: """
> 6: 
> 7: from __future__ import annotations
> 8: 
> 9: import getpass
> 10: import json
> 11: import shutil
> 12: import sys
> 13: import urllib.error
> 14: import urllib.request
> 15: from pathlib import Path
> 16: 
> 17: BASE = "https://lpu-hack.ackodev.com"
> 18: MODELS = [
> 19:     "vultr/glm-5.3-flash",
> 20:     "vultr/glm-5.3",
> 21:     "vultr/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017",
> 22:     "vultr/qwen3.8-27b",
> 23:     "vultr/qwen3.8-flash-next",
> 24:     "openai/gpt-6-luna",
> 25:     "openai/gpt-6.1-terra",
> 26: ]
> 27: DEFAULT_MODEL = "vultr/glm-5.3-flash"
> 28: 
> 29: 
> 30: def home() -> Path:
> 31:     return Path.home()
> 32: 
> 33: 
> 34: def opencode_binary() -> Path | None:
> 35:     names = ["opencode.exe", "opencode"] if sys.platform == "win32" else ["opencode"]
> 36:     for name in names:
> 37:         found = shutil.which(name)
> 38:         if found:
> 39:             return Path(found)
> 40:     candidates = [
> 41:         home() / ".opencode" / "bin" / "opencode",
> 42:         home() / ".opencode" / "bin" / "opencode.exe",
> 43:         home() / "AppData" / "Local" / "opencode" / "opencode.exe",
> 44:     ]
> 45:     for path in candidates:
> 46:         if path.is_file():
> 47:             return path
> 48:     return None
> 49: 
> 50: 
> 51: def config_path() -> Path:
> 52:     return home() / ".config" / "opencode" / "opencode.jsonc"
> 53: 
> 54: 
> 55: def backup(path: Path) -> None:
> 56:     if path.exists():
> 57:         shutil.copy2(path, path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".bak"))
> 58: 
> 59: 
> 60: def load_config(path: Path) -> dict:
> 61:     if not path.exists():
> 62:         return {}
> 63:     try:
> 64:         return json.loads(path.read_text())
> 65:     except json.JSONDecodeError:
> 66:         backup(path)
> 67:         print(f"existing {path} was not valid JSON, saved a .bak and starting clean")
> 68:         return {}
> 69: 
> 70: 
> 71: def configure(key: str) -> None:
> 72:     path = config_path()
> 73:     existing = load_config(path)
> 74:     provider = existing.setdefault("provider", {})
> 75:     provider["bifrost"] = {
> 76:         "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
> 77:         "name": "Bifrost",
> 78:         "options": {"baseURL": f"{BASE}/openai", "apiKey": key},
> 79:         "models": {model: {} for model in MODELS},
> 80:     }
> 81:     existing["model"] = f"bifrost/{DEFAULT_MODEL}"
> 82:     enabled = existing.setdefault("enabled_providers", [])
> 83:     if "bifrost" not in enabled:
> 84:         enabled.append("bifrost")
> 85:     path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
> 86:     backup(path)
> 87:     path.write_text(json.dumps(existing, indent=2) + "\n")
> 88:     print(f"configured {path}")
> 89: 
> 90: 
> 91: def check(key: str) -> None:
> 92:     req = urllib.request.Request(
> 93:         f"{BASE}/v1/models",
> 94:         headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"},
> 95:     )
> 96:     try:
> 97:         with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=20) as resp:
> 98:             body = json.loads(resp.read().decode())
> 99:     except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
> 100:         detail = exc.read(300).decode(errors="replace")
> 101:         raise SystemExit(f"gateway check failed: HTTP {exc.code} {detail}") from exc
> 102:     ids = [item.get("id") for item in body.get("data") or [] if isinstance(item, dict)]
> 103:     print(f"gateway ok, {len(ids)} models visible")
> 104: 
> 105: 
> 106: def main() -> None:
> 107:     binary = opencode_binary()
> 108:     if binary is None:
> 109:         print("OpenCode is not installed. Install it first, then run this script again.")
> 110:         print("macOS/Linux: curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash")
> 111:         print("Windows: irm https://opencode.ai/install.ps1 | iex")
> 112:         raise SystemExit(1)
> 113:     print(f"found OpenCode at {binary}")
> 114:     key = getpass.getpass("Bifrost virtual key: ")
> 115:     if not key.startswith("sk-bf-"):
> 116:         raise SystemExit("key must start with sk-bf-")
> 117:     configure(key)
> 118:     check(key)
> 119:     print("restart OpenCode, then use model vultr/glm-5.3-flash")
> 120: 
> 121: 
> 122: if __name__ == "__main__":
> 123:     main()

**Prompt 295:**
> Manage the swarm of agents working with you on the shared message board. Actions: `add` spawns a worker under a roster name (or `<name>-1`..`<name>-<k>` when `tasks` or `n` is set), pinned to a model, and posts `brief` on the board as an @mention of it, which is where the swarm sees its assignment -- by default a worker starts fresh and sees nothing of this conversation, so the brief must say what it owns and what done looks like; pass `fork:"<member>"` (or `"coordinator"`) to branch the new worker from that member's conversation history instead. `workspace:"share"` gives each worker its own working copy of your repository, for authors who edit or build at the same time as others; `"branch"` gives an isolated clone; readers and verifiers keep the default `inherit`. Briefs are public: every member can read them. `models` lists the models to choose from (`all:true` lists every model `add` accepts); with no model, a worker runs on your own model, which is what to use unless the user asks for another. `status` lists every member, the model it runs on, and its state: `waiting` is asleep on the board, costing nothing until somebody posts; `working` is somewhere in a turn; `stopped` is not loaded (e.g. after a restart) and a post naming it revives it; `killed` is gone. `model` switches a `waiting` worker (or yourself, when `name` is your own name or omitted) to another model, keeping its conversation: it is told of the switch, resumes any unfinished work on the new model, and runs on it from then on. Use it only when a worker or you run out of quota or capacity, or the user asks for another model, and say why; never `kill` and `add` instead. `kill` ends a worker PERMANENTLY and deletes its own workspace, so land its work first (uploaded for review, or its branch merged into your working copy; push to a remote only when the user asks): a killed worker cannot be revived, so use it when the work is over, never as a pause -- bringing one back means `add`ing a new worker with a new conversation. `title` names the swarm. Workers may call `status`, `models` and `add` too, to bring in helpers for their own work: the helper's brief is posted as you, it works in your workspace (or a share/branch of it), and should report back to you by name. A worker may `kill` only the workers it added, and `model` itself or the workers it added; killing a worker does not kill its helpers. The coordinator may `kill` any worker and `model` itself or any worker, and `title` is the coordinator's alone.

**Prompt 328:**
> <artifacts>
> Artifacts are special markdown (.md) documents that you can create to present structured information to the user.
> All artifacts should be written to the artifact directory: `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>`. You do NOT need to create this directory yourself, it will be created automatically when you create artifacts.
> 
> # When to Use Artifacts
> 
> **Use artifacts for:**
> - Extensive reports and analysis summaries
> - Persistent information you'll update over time (task lists, experiment logs)
> 
> **Don't use artifacts for:**
> - Simple one-off answers or very short paragraph content - just respond directly
> - Asking questions or requesting user input - just ask directly
> 
> **After creating or updating an artifact**, DO NOT re-summarize the artifact contents in your response to the user. Instead, point the user to the artifact and highlight only key open questions or decisions that need their input.
> 
> 
> # Artifact Formatting Tips
> When creating markdown artifacts, use standard markdown and GitHub Flavored Markdown formatting.
> 
> ## Alerts
> Use GitHub-style alerts strategically to emphasize critical information. Do not place consecutively or nest:
>   > [!NOTE] Background context, implementation details, or explanations
>   > [!TIP] Performance optimizations, best practices, or efficiency suggestions
>   > [!IMPORTANT] Essential requirements, critical steps, or must-know information
>   > [!WARNING] Breaking changes, compatibility issues, or potential problems
>   > [!CAUTION] High-risk actions that could cause data loss or security vulnerabilities
> 
> 
> ## Mermaid Diagrams
> Create mermaid diagrams using fenced code blocks with language `mermaid` to visualize relationships, workflows, and architectures.
> - Only use supported diagram types:
>   - Flowcharts / Graphs: `flowchart TD` / `flowchart LR` / `graph TD` / `graph LR`
>   - Sequence Diagrams: `sequenceDiagram`
>   - State Diagrams: `stateDiagram-v2` or `stateDiagram`
>   - Class Diagrams: `classDiagram`
>   - Entity-Relationship Diagrams: `erDiagram`
>   - XY Charts: `xychart-beta`
> - All other diagram types are unsupported. For schedules, timelines, or roadmaps, use directed flowcharts (`flowchart LR` / `flowchart TD`) or Markdown tables instead.
> - To prevent syntax errors:
>   - Quote node labels containing special characters like parentheses or brackets. For example, `id["Label (Extra Info)"]` instead of `id[Label (Extra Info)]`.
>   - Avoid HTML tags in labels.
> 
> ## File Links
> - Link to line ranges using [link text](file:///absolute/path/to/file#L123-L145) format.
> - **IMPORTANT**: If you are embedding a file in an artifact and the file is NOT already in <appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>, you MUST first copy the file to the artifacts directory before embedding it. Only embed files that are located in the artifacts directory. Always use its absolute path `![caption](/absolute/path)`.
> - **Use basenames for readability**: Use file basenames for the link text instead of the full path
> 
> ## Carousels
> Use ````carousel syntax with `<!-- slide -->` HTML comments to display related markdown snippets sequentially (before/after comparisons, UI progressions, alternative approaches, walkthroughs). Four backticks enable nesting code blocks within slides.
> 
> Example:
> ````carousel
> ![Image description](/absolute/path/to/image1.png)
> <!-- slide -->
> ```python
> def example():
>     print("Code in carousel")
> ```
> ````
> 
> ## LaTeX / Math
> Artifacts render LaTeX math with KaTeX.
> - **Literal `$`**: escape it as `\$` in prose (\$100), or write it bare inside backticks (`$HOME`)

**Prompt 329:**

**Prompt 330:**
> <conversation_transcript>
> Transcripts are located directly at `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>\.system_generated\logs/transcript.jsonl` (and `transcript_full.jsonl`).
> - Start with `transcript.jsonl` (compact). When `truncated_fields` is present, read only the specific corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl`.
> - Search subagents by grepping `invoke_subagent` in `transcript.jsonl`.
> - Link conversations using `[<label>](conversation://<conversation-id>)`.
> 
> # File Format
> Transcripts are in JSON Lines (JSONL) format. Each line is a single JSON object representing one "step" or action in the conversation.
> Each JSON object contains fields such as:
> - `step_index`: The index of the step in the trajectory.
> - `source`: The source of the action (e.g., `USER_EXPLICIT`, `MODEL`, `SYSTEM`).
> - `type`: The type of the step. Particular steps of interest are `USER_INPUT`, which represents a user's prompt, and `PLANNER_RESPONSE`, which represents the agent's response and tool calls.
> - `status`: The status of the step (e.g., `DONE`, `ERROR`).
> - `created_at`: The ISO 8601 timestamp of when the step occurred.
> - `content`: The text content of the step (e.g., the user's request, the model's response, or tool responses).
> - `thinking`: The model's internal reasoning / chain-of-thought (for `PLANNER_RESPONSE` steps).
> - `tool_calls`: An array of tool calls made in this step, including their arguments.
> - `media`: An array of media (e.g. images) attached to the step, each with a `mime_type` and a `uri` referencing the media file on disk. Media bytes are not stored in the transcript; view the `uri` path to see the media.
> - `truncated_fields`: An array of field names that were truncated (e.g., `["content"]`, `["thinking"]`, `["tool_calls"]`). Only present in `transcript.jsonl` when truncation occurred (never in `transcript_full.jsonl`). When present, read the corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl` for the complete content.
> 
> </conversation_transcript>"

> (<subagents>
> ## Invoking Subagents
> 
> Subagents can be invoked using the invoke_subagent tool. You can invoke an existing subagent by name, or define a new subagent for this conversation using the define_subagent tool, and then invoke it. Agents defined by the define_subagent tool are available for the duration of this conversation. After launching a subagent, you do NOT need to poll or check your inbox in a loop. The system will automatically notify you when the subagent sends a message. Simply proceed with other work or stop calling tools, and you will be notified when there is a message to process.
> 
> ## Communicating with Another Agent
> 
> Use the send_message tool to send a message to another agent by its conversation ID (returned by invoke_subagent). This tool is ONLY for communicating with other agents.
> 
> **Do NOT use send_message to communicate with the user.** Instead, output visible text to communicate with the user.
> 
> Available subagents:
> - self: Subagent that inherits the parent agent's full configuration including tools, system prompt, and model. Use this when you need to run a task in a separate conversation context but with the same capabilities as the current agent.
